Accountable obligation owner.value: Controller owns the group risk-and-control matrix over financial reporting; the independent assurance line demanded by ICP 8.8 sits with the Chief Audit Executive reporting direct to the Audit Committee

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 8 Standards 8.3 and 8.8 and ICP 7 Standard 7.11 read against the current consolidated ICP text on iaisweb.org, then cross-walked to the local implementations actually relied on: NAIC Model Audit Rule 205 Sections 11 and 16, Solvency II Directive Articles 46 (internal control) and 47 (internal audit), OSFI Guideline E-13

In-scope processes.value: Statutory and IFRS financial close for every consolidated insurance and holding entity: premium and policy-liability recording, reinsurance ceded accounting, investment valuation, DAC, expense accrual, intercompany elimination, consolidation and disclosure

In-scope systems.value: General ledger and sub-ledgers plus the close and consolidation stack; the risk-and-control matrix, control attributes and performance evidence are held in the GRC platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Group ICFR Framework and Risk & Control Matrix Procedure — scoping and materiality, process-level control design, ITGC scope, evidence standards, deficiency rating scale, quarterly sub-certification cycle

Compliance procedure approved.value: Framework approved by the Chief Financial Officer and noted by the Audit Committee annually; the internal audit charter carrying the ICP 8.8 direct reporting line is approved by the Audit Committee itself, not by management

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Controls operate continuously with a quarterly sub-certification cycle closing on working day 12; management report on internal control over financial reporting is due 1 August after year end under Model Audit Rule Section 16, and the system-of-governance description feeds the group SFCR at 14 weeks after year end

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC platform emails each control owner 10 business days before the control due date, escalates any unperformed key control to the Controller at due date plus 3 business days, and opens sub-certification tasks on working day 5 after each quarter close

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Control matrix versions, control performance evidence, sub-certifications and deficiency logs retained 7 years from the financial period end in the compliance evidence repository, indexed by legal entity, process and control id

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Failed, unperformed or late key controls are raised as deficiencies rated inconsequential / significant deficiency / material weakness, each with owner, remediation date and a recorded retest result

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CAE validates remediation of every significant deficiency and material weakness and reports closure directly to the Audit Committee

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All key controls in the group risk-and-control matrix that operated during the financial year across every consolidated entity, plus the ITGC population for the general ledger, policy administration, actuarial valuation and consolidation systems

Pass/fail thresholds.value: A key control fails if evidence of any single operation is missing, performed outside its frequency window, or lacks a named reviewer and date; any material weakness, or a key-control failure rate above 5 percent at entity level, forces a not-effective ICFR conclusion for that entity

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous, so control operation is monitored monthly, high-risk process controls are tested at interim each quarter, and every key control is tested at least once a year with a year-end roll-forward

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: No auditor may test a control performed by their own function; Finance staff test no Finance-operated control

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual ICFR testing workpaper set — scoping memo, RCM extract, sample listing, re-performance notes, deficiency log — held in AuditBoard and cross-referenced from the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Control matrix, testing results and the Section 16 management report producible for a group-wide supervisor or supervisory college request, or a state financial condition examination, within 10 business days in NAIC Financial Condition Examiners Handbook exhibit format

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager coordinates examiner and group-wide supervisor requests; the CFO clears any statement about a material weakness before it leaves the company and the Audit Committee chair is told the same day

checklist.step: Refresh the ICFR scope and materiality for the financial year
actions: Export the prior-year trial balance by legal entity from the general ledger Financial Statement Version, one row per account and entity, for every consolidated insurance and holding company.

Set group planning materiality on the stated basis (working rule for an insurer: the lower of 5 percent of pre-tax income and 0.5 percent of total assets) and push performance materiality down to each entity at 60 to 75 percent of that figure.

Mark an account in scope where its balance exceeds entity performance materiality or it is judgemental — policy liabilities, IBNR, DAC, reinsurance recoverables, level 2 and level 3 investment fair values, deferred tax.
Ask the Appointed Actuary which reserve segments carry the widest estimation uncertainty and pull those segments into scope regardless of balance size.
Save the signed and dated scoping memo as tab 1 of the control matrix workbook and attach it to the GRC scoping record.
checklist.done: the scoping memo names the in-scope entities, accounts and processes together with the materiality figures each was selected against.

checklist.step: Map every in-scope account to a process and a control objective
actions: In the GRC platform open Risk ▸ Process Hierarchy and create or confirm a process row for each cycle: premium and receivables, claims and reserves, ceded reinsurance, investments, expenses and payroll, tax, consolidation and disclosure.
Attach each in-scope account from the scoping memo to exactly one process so no material account is orphaned and none is double-counted.

For each process write the financial statement assertions at risk — existence, completeness, valuation, rights and obligations, presentation — and state the what-could-go-wrong in one sentence per assertion.
Walk each process end to end with the process owner and record the systems, hand-offs and manual journal points in a narrative attached to the process row.
checklist.done: every in-scope account maps to one process, and each process carries a written what-could-go-wrong per assertion plus a walkthrough narrative.

checklist.step: Document the control design in the risk-and-control matrix
actions: Create one matrix row per control carrying: control id, process, assertion covered, control description, preventive or detective, manual or automated, frequency, performer role, reviewer role, evidence artifact and system of record.

Write the control description so it states who does what, against what source, to what threshold — for example reconciles the premium sub-ledger to GL account 4100 monthly and investigates every difference above 25,000.
Flag as key any control that alone covers a material assertion, and confirm every assertion in every in-scope process has at least one key control.
Send the draft matrix to each process owner for confirmation that the control as written matches what they actually perform, and correct the wording rather than the practice where they differ.
checklist.done: each in-scope assertion is covered by at least one key control whose description names the performer, source, threshold and evidence.

checklist.step: Evidence the ICP 8.3 control functions and their charters
actions: Collect the current charter for each control function ICP 8 expects to exist — risk management, compliance, actuarial and internal audit — from the board portal governance library.
Check each charter states the function head, the board committee it reports to, its unrestricted right of access to records and staff, and its resourcing and budget authority.
Record the board or committee approval date and minute reference for each charter and flag any charter older than the annual review cycle.
Confirm with the Corporate Secretary that the current organisation chart shows each function head with a reporting line that does not run only through the business it reviews.
File the charter set plus the approval references as the ICP 8.3 evidence pack for the year.
checklist.done: all four control-function charters are current, board-approved with a dated minute reference, and show an unimpaired reporting line.

checklist.step: Confirm internal audit independence and the direct board reporting line
actions: Confirm in the internal audit charter that the CAE reports functionally to the Audit Committee, that the committee approves CAE appointment, removal and remuneration, and that the audit plan cannot be amended by management alone — the ICP 8.8 and ICP 7.11 conditions.

Build the risk-based annual audit plan from the group risk register and the ICFR matrix and take it to the Audit Committee for approval, showing the coverage of each material process over a rolling three-year cycle.
Log the private sessions held between the CAE and the Audit Committee without management present, with dates, in the board portal minutes index.
Complete and file annual independence declarations for the CAE and every auditor covering operational responsibilities held in the last twelve months.
Report to the committee any instance where access to records, systems or people was restricted, naming who restricted it.
checklist.done: a committee-approved risk-based audit plan, dated private sessions and signed independence declarations are on file, with any access restriction reported.

checklist.step: Assign control owners and enforce preparer and reviewer segregation
actions: Name a single accountable performer and a separate reviewer on every matrix row and reject any row where the two are the same person.

Run the segregation-of-duties ruleset in the IAM platform against the ERP roles held by each named performer, testing at minimum journal-entry post versus approve, vendor create versus payment release, and reserve set versus reserve approve.
Send every conflict hit to the entitlement owner for removal or, where the business insists, a documented compensating control and a dated CFO exception approval.
Refresh the named-owner list after each organisation change so a leaver never remains the recorded control owner.
checklist.done: every control has distinct named performer and reviewer, and every open segregation conflict is either removed or covered by a dated CFO exception.

checklist.step: Scope and document the IT general controls behind the financial systems
actions: List the systems that produce or hold financial reporting data: general ledger, consolidation tool, policy administration, claims platform, actuarial valuation platform and the investment accounting feed.

For each system document the four ITGC domains — logical access provisioning and revocation, privileged access, change management, and job scheduling and backup — naming the control, the performer and the evidence.
Schedule the user access review at least half-yearly per system in the IAM platform, with the certification campaign owner set to the business application owner rather than IT.
Confirm developers hold no standing write access to production financial data and that emergency access runs through a break-glass account with a ticketed after-the-fact review.
checklist.done: each financial system has documented access, privileged-access, change and scheduling controls with a scheduled recertification campaign.

checklist.step: Load the matrix into the GRC platform and schedule control performance
actions: Import the completed matrix into the GRC control library, mapping each column to the platform fields so control id, frequency, owner and evidence type are queryable.
Set the recurrence on every control row — daily, monthly at working day 5, quarterly, annual — and let the platform generate the performance tasks rather than tracking them in a spreadsheet.
Configure the reminder at 10 business days before due and the Controller escalation at due plus 3 business days.
Attach the assertion mapping and the ICP 8 and Model Audit Rule references to each control so a supervisor can be shown the requirement behind any control.
checklist.done: every control exists in the GRC library with a recurrence, an owner, reminders and a citation mapping, and no key control is tracked outside the platform.

checklist.step: Operate and evidence the close controls each month
actions: Work the close task list in order, completing each balance sheet reconciliation with the sub-ledger or custodian statement attached as the supporting document.
Investigate and clear every reconciling item above the account threshold before certifying, and record ageing and an owner for anything left open.
Route each reconciliation for reviewer approval so the platform captures reviewer name and timestamp rather than an initialled printout.
Attach the manual journal support to each above-threshold journal and confirm the approver differs from the preparer.
Hand the completed close pack and the exceptions list to the Controller on working day 8.
checklist.done: every in-scope account is reconciled, reviewed with a system-captured approver and timestamp, and open items carry an age and an owner.

checklist.step: Cover the actuarial and investment valuation controls
actions: Reconcile the seriatim policy extract feeding the valuation run to the policy administration in-force counts and face amounts, and document every difference above the reconciliation tolerance.
Record the model version, assumption set version and run id for each valuation run so a reserve balance can be traced to a reproducible run.
Have a second actuary independently review assumption changes and the movement analysis from prior period, signing the movement walk before the reserve posts to the ledger.
Agree the investment fair value hierarchy classification and level 3 valuations with the Investment Analyst, retaining the pricing source and any manager override rationale.
Post the reserve and valuation journals with the run id in the journal reference so the ledger balance links back to the model output.
checklist.done: reserve and investment balances in the ledger trace to a named model run and assumption set, with an independent reviewer signature on the movement analysis.

checklist.step: Reconcile control coverage across the local statutory frameworks
actions: List every reporting basis the group files on — NAIC statutory annual statement, IFRS 17 group accounts, Solvency II QRTs and SFCR, LICAT or MCT returns, BMA economic balance sheet — and the entity behind each.
For every basis-specific adjustment (statutory to GAAP, IFRS 17 CSM roll-forward, Solvency II best estimate and risk margin) confirm a control exists over the adjustment calculation and its review.
Confirm the conversion or mapping bridge between bases is itself controlled and version-managed rather than sitting in an untracked spreadsheet.
Note where a local supervisor imposes an additional control requirement and record the added control row and its owner in the matrix.
checklist.done: each reporting basis and each basis conversion has a named control in the matrix with an owner and evidence.

checklist.step: Rate control deficiencies and route them to remediation
actions: Raise a deficiency record the moment a key control is missed, performed late or performed without evidence, capturing the control id, period affected and the accounts exposed.

Rate the severity against the stated scale — inconsequential, significant deficiency, material weakness — using the magnitude of the potential misstatement and the likelihood, not the actual error found.
Assign a remediation owner and a date, and specify whether the fix is redesign, re-training or an added compensating control.
Escalate every significant deficiency to the CFO within 5 business days and every material weakness to the Audit Committee chair the same day it is rated.
checklist.done: each deficiency has a severity rating with a stated magnitude and likelihood basis, an owner, a remediation date and evidence of the required escalation.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly sub-certification cycle
actions: Open sub-certification tasks in the GRC platform on working day 5 after quarter close for every process owner and entity finance lead.

Require each certifier to state that the controls they own operated as designed, to list any control missed and any known unrecorded misstatement, and to confirm nothing has been withheld from the auditors.
Chase non-responders at working day 9 and report any certification refused or qualified to the CFO before the results roll up.
Roll the sub-certifications into the group representation supporting the CFO and CEO sign-off on the quarter.
checklist.done: every process owner and entity finance lead has certified or explicitly qualified, and all qualifications reached the CFO before group sign-off.

checklist.step: Draft the management report on internal control over financial reporting and take it to the committee
actions: Draft the Model Audit Rule Section 16 management report stating the framework used, that management is responsible for ICFR, the assessment conclusion, and any unremediated material weakness — due to the domiciliary regulator by 1 August after year end.
Reconcile the conclusion to the deficiency log so no rated material weakness is omitted from the statement.
Present the report, the annual testing results and the internal audit opinion to the Audit Committee via the board portal ahead of the meeting, and minute the committee's acceptance.
Have the report signed by the CFO and the officer responsible for financial reporting and lodged with the annual audited financial report filing.
checklist.done: a signed management report reconciled to the deficiency log has been accepted by the Audit Committee and lodged by the 1 August deadline.

checklist.step: Retain the control matrix and the year evidence set
actions: Move the year-end frozen control matrix, all control performance evidence, sub-certifications, deficiency logs and the Section 16 report into the compliance evidence repository under the financial year folder.
Apply the 7-years-from-period-end retention label and set the record to legal-hold-eligible so an examination can freeze it.
Confirm the repository index makes the pack searchable by legal entity, process, control id and financial year.
Record the frozen matrix version number in the GRC platform so later changes cannot silently overwrite what was tested.
checklist.done: the frozen matrix and evidence pack is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by entity, control id and year.

testing.step: Build the population of key controls that operated in the year
actions: Export from the GRC control library every control flagged key with an operation date inside the financial year, with entity, process, frequency, owner and expected operation count.
Compute the expected instance count per control from its frequency and compare it to the tasks actually generated, so a control switched off mid-year is visible.
Add the ITGC control population for the ledger, consolidation, policy administration and actuarial valuation systems.
Sign the extract as complete, recording the extract date, filter criteria and record count in the workpaper header.
testing.done: the key-control population is extracted, expected-versus-generated instance counts are reconciled, and the extract is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the control matrix back to the financial statements
actions: Pull the year-end trial balance by entity and total the balances of accounts marked in scope in the matrix.
Compute the percentage of total assets, total liabilities and total revenue covered by in-scope accounts and challenge any coverage below the framework threshold.
List every account above entity performance materiality that carries no control in the matrix and treat each as a scoping exception.
Check the judgemental accounts named by the Appointed Actuary are all in scope irrespective of size.
testing.done: coverage percentages are computed and every material or judgemental account without a mapped control is listed as a scoping exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100 percent of controls over policy liabilities, reinsurance recoverables and consolidation, and every control with a prior-year deficiency.
Select the remaining sample by frequency-based sample sizes — 2 instances for annual and quarterly controls, 5 for monthly, 25 for daily — using a seeded random draw.
Record the seed, population size, sample size per control and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Add a roll-forward sample of instances after the interim testing cut-off for any control tested at interim.
testing.done: the sample is drawn to stated frequency-based sizes, is reproducible from the recorded seed, and covers all prior-year deficient controls.

testing.step: Re-perform the sampled controls rather than inspecting the sign-off
actions: For each sampled reconciliation, pull the sub-ledger and GL balances as at the control date yourself and re-derive the difference before opening the performer's workpaper.
Confirm the reviewer identity and review timestamp come from the system rather than a typed name, and that the review post-dates the preparation.
Test the investigation of reconciling items: pick two items above threshold and follow the stated resolution to the supporting document.
Record any control that is evidenced only by a signature with no underlying support as a design failure, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: each sampled control has an independent re-performance note showing the auditor derived the result before reading the performer's answer.

testing.step: Test the IT general controls behind the sampled financial systems
actions: Pull the current entitlement extract for the ledger, consolidation and valuation systems and test the leaver population against the HR termination list for access still active more than 5 business days after the leave date.
Select 15 changes released to the financial systems in the year and trace each to an approved change ticket, a test result and a deployer different from the developer.
Test the privileged-access population for named individual accounts, and follow every break-glass use to a ticket and an after-the-fact review.
Confirm the half-yearly access certification campaigns completed and that revocations requested were actioned.
testing.done: leaver access, change approval, privileged access and certification completion are each tested with results recorded per system.

testing.step: Verify the ICP 8 governance conditions independently
actions: Read the internal audit charter and confirm in the text itself that appointment, removal and remuneration of the CAE sit with the Audit Committee, as ICP 8.8 and ICP 7.11 require.
Trace the approved risk-based audit plan to the committee minutes and check delivered coverage against planned coverage, listing any audit deferred without committee approval.
Count the private sessions between the committee and the CAE, the external auditor and the Appointed Actuary in the year, and flag any where none was held.
Confirm charters for the risk, compliance and actuarial functions were reviewed inside the annual cycle and that each names a board reporting line.
testing.done: charter wording, plan-versus-delivered coverage and private session counts are verified against the minutes, with deferrals and gaps listed.

testing.step: Recompute the materiality and coverage maths behind the scope
actions: Recompute group planning materiality from the audited figures using the framework basis and compare it to the figure used for scoping.
Recompute the pushed-down entity performance materiality at the stated percentage and identify entities scoped out on a materiality figure that is now too high.
Recompute the coverage percentages and check they reconcile to the coverage stated in the scoping memo.
Where the recomputed materiality would have pulled a further entity or account into scope, list it as a scoping exception with the balance involved.
testing.done: materiality and coverage are recomputed from audited figures and every entity or account that should have been in scope is listed with its balance.

testing.step: Trace deficiency remediation from raise to retest
actions: Extract every deficiency raised in the year and the prior year with its rating, owner, remediation date and status.
For each closed significant deficiency and material weakness, find the retest evidence and confirm the retest covered instances after the fix date, not before it.

Check the required escalations happened on time — CFO within 5 business days for significant deficiencies, Audit Committee chair same day for material weaknesses — using the dated notification records.
List any deficiency closed on assertion alone, with no retest evidence, as an exception.
testing.done: every closed significant deficiency and material weakness has post-fix retest evidence and a dated escalation record, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the control id, entity, period, what failed and the accounts and assertions exposed.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — scoping gap, control not performed, evidence not retained, segregation conflict, ITGC failure, model or assumption change uncontrolled — and name a single owner.
Set a remediation date and mark whether the exception changes the entity ICFR conclusion under the 5 percent failure threshold.
Carry every open exception into the next year plan as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue record, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the ICFR test
actions: Compute the key-control failure rate per entity and compare it to the 5 percent threshold and to the presence of any material weakness.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or not effective — per entity and for the group, citing the workpaper references behind each.
Have the independent reviewer, who tested no control performed by their own function, sign the workpaper set.

Report the conclusion and any unremediated material weakness to the Audit Committee at its next sitting, confirm it agrees with the Section 16 management report, and file the pack in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the failure rate and conclusion per entity, agrees to the Section 16 report, and is reported to the Audit Committee and filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: CAE owns the annual key-control test plan and the remediation follow-up register; first-line control owners named in each finding own the fixes

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 22 Standard 22.3 (risk-based AML/CFT approach) and ICP 15 Standards 15.6 to 15.8 (investment risk management and derivatives) read against the current consolidated ICP text, and cross-walked to FATF Recommendation 1, the NAIC Derivatives Use Plan requirement under the Investments of Insurers Model Act, and Solvency II Article 132 prudent person principle

In-scope processes.value: The key controls over the two areas the cited standards drive: AML/CFT customer risk rating, enhanced and simplified due diligence, sanctions and PEP screening and suspicious activity escalation; and investment and derivative controls covering the derivatives use plan, hedge documentation, counterparty and collateral limits and admitted asset limits

In-scope systems.value: AML case and risk-rating engine plus the sanctions screening system for ICP 22 controls, and the investment book of record and Schedule DB derivative records for ICP 15 controls; audit results are held in AuditBoard

Compliance procedure documented.value: Internal Audit Testing and Remediation Procedure — annual plan derivation from the risk assessment, test attribute design, sample sizing, evidence standards, finding rating scale, management action agreement and retest rules

Compliance procedure approved.value: Test plan and procedure approved by the Audit Committee at the start of the audit year; any in-year plan change needs the committee chair, not management, to approve it

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual test cycle: plan approved by the committee before the audit year starts, fieldwork closed and findings issued within 30 calendar days of test completion, management actions agreed within 15 business days of the draft report, high findings retested within 90 days of their stated remediation date

Deadline reminders configured.value: AuditBoard issue tracker emails the action owner at 30, 15 and 5 days before the remediation date and escalates to the CAE and the accountable executive on the day an action goes overdue

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Test plans, attribute sheets, sample listings, re-performance evidence, findings and retest evidence retained 7 years from report issue in AuditBoard, mirrored to the compliance evidence repository by audit year

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Each control failure becomes a rated finding — high, medium, low — with root cause, agreed management action, owner, due date and a recorded retest outcome of closed-verified or reopened

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Only the CAE closes a high or medium finding, and only on retest evidence covering instances after the fix date

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All key controls scheduled in the approved annual audit plan over the AML/CFT and investment/derivative areas, plus every finding open at the start of the year and every finding raised during it

Pass/fail thresholds.value: A control passes only if every sampled instance meets every stated attribute; one attribute failure in a sample of monthly controls is a finding, any failure of a sanctions screening or derivative authorisation control is automatically rated high, and any finding closed without post-fix retest evidence is a quality failure of the audit itself

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual quality review workpaper — plan coverage analysis, re-performed samples, finding rating challenge, remediation trace — filed in the compliance evidence repository under the audit year alongside the AuditBoard export
