checklist.step: Build the annual key-control test plan from the risk assessment
actions: Pull the current enterprise risk assessment and the AML/CFT enterprise-wide risk assessment and rank the auditable units by inherent risk and time since last audit.

Schedule into the plan every control that alone covers a cited standard — customer risk rating and due diligence under ICP 22.3, and the derivatives use plan, counterparty limits and investment limit monitoring under ICP 15.6 to 15.8.
Set the audit hours, lead auditor and fieldwork window per audit and check no auditor is assigned to an area they worked in during the last twelve months.
Take the plan to the Audit Committee for approval before the audit year opens and record the minute reference in AuditBoard.
Publish the coverage map showing which ICP standard each planned audit evidences.
checklist.done: the committee has approved a risk-ranked plan whose coverage map names an audit against each cited ICP standard.

checklist.step: Confirm the AML/CFT risk assessment methodology the controls rest on
actions: Obtain the current enterprise-wide ML and TF risk assessment and check it separately scores the four dimensions ICP 22.3 names — customers, products, distribution channels and geographies.

Confirm the product scoring reflects insurance-specific exposure: single-premium and lump-sum investment contracts, free-look and early-surrender cash-out, third-party premium payment and assignment of benefit.
Confirm geography scoring uses a named source — FATF grey and black lists plus the sanctions programme list — with the version date recorded.
Check the assessment states which risk bands trigger enhanced due diligence and which permit simplified measures, and that the bands feed the risk-rating engine configuration.
Record the board or risk committee approval date and reject the assessment as evidence if it is more than twelve months old.
checklist.done: a board-approved risk assessment less than twelve months old scores all four ICP 22.3 dimensions and maps its bands to the due diligence measures actually applied.

checklist.step: Test customer risk rating and the proportionate due diligence applied
actions: Extract every policy issued in the year with its assigned customer risk band, product, premium mode and country of residence and payment.
Select 40 cases stratified across high, medium and low bands and re-derive the band from the risk assessment rules before opening the file.
For each high-risk case confirm the enhanced measures actually on file — source of funds and source of wealth evidence, senior management approval to onboard, and the shortened periodic review cycle.
For each simplified-measures case confirm the file evidences why the low-risk conditions were met rather than defaulting to simplified because the premium was small.
Record every band that differs from your re-derivation as a finding, including cases rated correctly by luck with no documented rationale.
checklist.done: 40 stratified cases have an independent re-derived risk band and evidence that the enhanced or simplified measures matching that band were applied.

checklist.step: Test sanctions and politically exposed person screening
actions: Confirm the screening system list versions and the date each was last refreshed, and check refresh happens within one business day of a list update.

Confirm the screened population covers policyholders, payers, beneficiaries, assignees and claim payees, not policyholders alone, and test the feed record counts against the policy administration issue counts.
Inject a set of known control names drawn from the sanctions list into a test run and confirm the system raises each one at the configured fuzzy-match threshold.
Sample 25 alerts closed as false positive and confirm each carries a documented discounting reason and a reviewer different from the person who raised it.
Check every true match was frozen, escalated and reported to the relevant authority within the local deadline and record the dates.
checklist.done: list currency, population completeness, match sensitivity and alert disposition are each tested, with the sample of closed alerts showing documented reasons and reviewer segregation.

checklist.step: Test suspicious activity identification, escalation and reporting
actions: Extract all internal suspicion reports raised in the year with the raise date, decision date and reporting outcome.

Recompute the reporting deadline for each report filed with the financial intelligence unit and compare it to the filing date, using the applicable local clock such as the 30-calendar-day suspicious activity report deadline.
Sample 15 reports closed without external filing and read the analyst rationale, testing whether the stated reason addresses the typology rather than repeating the transaction description.
Check that the tipping-off control held — that no customer communication after the report references the report.
Confirm the annual training completion record covers every staff member in a customer-facing or payment-releasing role.
checklist.done: every filed report is inside its recomputed deadline, no-file decisions carry a reasoned rationale, and training coverage is evidenced for all in-scope staff.

checklist.step: Test the investment policy and derivatives use plan controls
actions: Obtain the board-approved investment policy statement and the derivatives use plan filed with or held for the domiciliary supervisor, and note the approval dates and the permitted strategies.
Confirm the plan states the permitted derivative purposes — hedging, income generation, replication, and whether any speculative use is prohibited — as ICP 15.7 expects.
Extract all derivative positions open during the year from the investment book of record and match each to a permitted purpose in the plan.
Flag any strategy traded that the plan does not name, and any position opened before the plan amendment that authorised it.
Confirm the plan was re-approved by the board inside the stated review cycle.
checklist.done: every derivative strategy traded in the year maps to a purpose in a currently board-approved derivatives use plan, or is recorded as a finding.

checklist.step: Test hedge documentation and effectiveness evidence
actions: Select 15 hedge relationships and confirm inception documentation exists dated on or before the trade date, naming the hedged item, the hedging instrument, the risk hedged and the effectiveness method.
Re-perform the effectiveness assessment for the period using the documented method and compare your result to the recorded one.
Trace the accounting treatment applied to the effectiveness conclusion, checking a failed hedge was moved out of hedge accounting in the period it failed.
For hedges of variable annuity or index-linked guarantees, reconcile the hedged liability sensitivity used to the actuarial model run id it came from.
Record any hedge documented after the trade date as a finding regardless of subsequent effectiveness.
checklist.done: each sampled hedge has inception-dated documentation, an independently recomputed effectiveness result, and accounting that follows the conclusion.

checklist.step: Test counterparty exposure and collateral controls
actions: Extract derivative exposure by counterparty and compare each to the single-counterparty limit in the investment policy, recomputing exposure on the stated basis such as mark to market plus add-on.
Confirm an executed master agreement and credit support annex exists per active counterparty in the contract repository, with the threshold, minimum transfer amount and eligible collateral recorded.
Reconcile collateral held and posted to the counterparty statements for two margin dates and follow every disputed amount to its resolution.
Check counterparty credit ratings were monitored and that a downgrade below the policy floor triggered the documented action within the stated window.
checklist.done: counterparty exposures are recomputed against limits, every active counterparty has an executed agreement, and collateral reconciles to counterparty statements on the tested dates.

checklist.step: Test investment limit monitoring and breach handling
actions: Re-run the compliance rule set in the investment book of record for four month-ends and compare the breaches it reports to the breaches recorded in the monitoring log.
Test the limits ICP 15.6 to 15.8 speak to: asset class caps, single-issuer concentration, credit quality floors, liquidity minimums, currency matching and derivative notional caps.
For each recorded breach follow the timeline from detection to notification to the Chief Investment Officer and to remediation, and compare it to the policy cure period.
Identify passive breaches caused by market movement and confirm they were still logged and cured rather than waived silently.
Confirm the statutory admitted asset limits were monitored separately from the internal policy limits.
checklist.done: re-run rule results reconcile to the monitoring log for four month-ends and every breach shows detection, notification and cure inside the policy window.

checklist.step: Write the test attributes and evidence standard before fieldwork closes
actions: For every control tested record the attribute sheet: what must exist, what must be checked, who must have reviewed it, and the timing tolerance for each attribute.
State the sample basis on the sheet — population size, selection method, seed, sample size and the rationale for the size chosen.
Attach the actual evidence inspected per sampled instance rather than referring to it, so a reviewer can re-perform without asking the auditee.
Record the auditor conclusion per attribute, not just per control, so a partial failure is visible.
checklist.done: each tested control has an attribute sheet, a stated sample basis, attached evidence per instance and an attribute-level conclusion.

checklist.step: Rate findings and agree management actions
actions: Rate each finding high, medium or low on the published scale using regulatory exposure, financial magnitude and likelihood, and rate any sanctions screening or unauthorised derivative failure high by rule.
Issue the draft report within 30 calendar days of fieldwork completion and hold a closing meeting with the accountable executive.
Require a written management action per finding naming the fix, the owner by name and the due date, and reject actions that only promise to review or to remind staff.
Escalate any finding management declines to accept to the Audit Committee with the residual risk stated, rather than downgrading the rating.
checklist.done: every finding is rated on the published scale and carries a named-owner action with a date, or is escalated to the committee as accepted risk.

checklist.step: Track remediation to closure and retest
actions: Maintain the open findings register with owner, due date, status and days overdue, refreshed at least monthly.
Retest every high finding within 90 days of its stated remediation date using instances that occurred after the fix date.
Reopen any finding whose retest fails and reset the due date with the accountable executive rather than extending the original one silently.
Report the overdue population by executive owner to the Audit Committee at every sitting.
checklist.done: high findings are retested on post-fix instances within 90 days, failures are reopened, and overdue items are reported by executive owner.

checklist.step: Report results and coverage to the Audit Committee
actions: Prepare the committee pack: plan versus delivered coverage, findings raised by rating and area, open and overdue findings, and the annual internal audit opinion on the control environment.
State explicitly whether the AML/CFT and investment areas received the planned coverage and explain any audit deferred.
Present in a private session without management for the part covering findings against executives.
Record the committee minute reference against the plan and the opinion in AuditBoard.
checklist.done: the committee has received coverage, findings and the annual opinion, including a private session, with the minute reference recorded.

checklist.step: Feed the results back into next year risk assessment
actions: Load each finding onto the risk register entry for the risk it evidences and raise the residual risk score where a key control was found ineffective.
Feed the AML findings into the next enterprise-wide ML and TF risk assessment refresh, specifically into the control effectiveness dimension.
Feed the investment findings into the next investment policy and derivatives use plan review with the Chief Investment Officer.
Record which findings changed a risk rating so next year plan derivation can be traced back to evidence.
checklist.done: every finding is linked to a risk register entry and the AML and investment assessments show the control effectiveness input from this year testing.

checklist.step: Retain the audit year evidence set
actions: Export the approved plan, attribute sheets, sample listings, evidence attachments, issued reports and retest evidence from AuditBoard at year end.
File the export in the compliance evidence repository under the audit year and apply the 7-years-from-report-issue retention label.
Confirm the pack is searchable by audit name, control id, finding id and ICP standard reference.
Lock the workpapers against edit once the report is issued so post-issue changes are only possible as a dated addendum.
checklist.done: the audit year pack is exported, filed with a 7-year label, searchable by finding and ICP reference, and locked against post-issue edits.

testing.step: Build the population of planned and delivered key-control tests
actions: Export the committee-approved annual audit plan with every planned audit, its scope statement and its target quarter.
Export every audit actually issued in the year with its issue date, scope and the controls tested.
Add the full finding population — opening balance, raised, closed, reopened, overdue at year end.
Reconcile planned to delivered and list every planned audit not delivered, with the recorded reason and who approved the deferral.
testing.done: planned and delivered audits are reconciled, every deferral has a recorded approver, and the finding population is complete.

testing.step: Reconcile coverage back to the risk assessment and the cited standards
actions: Take the top-quartile risks from the enterprise and AML risk assessments and check each has an audit in the plan or a documented reason it does not.
Trace the coverage map claim that ICP 22.3 and ICP 15.6 to 15.8 were covered to the actual scope statements of the delivered audits.
Flag any area claimed as covered where the delivered scope tested only design and not operating effectiveness.
List uncovered high risks with the number of years since they were last audited.
testing.done: each cited standard traces to a delivered audit that tested operating effectiveness, and uncovered high risks are listed with their years since last audit.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of tested controls and findings
actions: Take 100 percent of the sanctions screening, customer risk rating and derivative authorisation control tests.
Take a seeded random sample of 15 further tested controls across the AML and investment audits.
Take 100 percent of high findings and a seeded sample of 10 medium findings closed in the year.
Record the seed, population sizes, sample sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from a recorded seed and includes every high-risk control test and every high finding.

testing.step: Re-perform the customer risk rating judgement independently
actions: Take 15 of the cases the auditor tested and re-derive the customer risk band from the risk assessment rules without reading the auditor conclusion.
Compare your band to both the business rating and the auditor conclusion and record any case where the auditor accepted a wrong band.
Check the enhanced due diligence evidence yourself for every high-band case in your sample, specifically source of funds and senior approval.
Treat an auditor conclusion of satisfactory on a case with no source-of-funds evidence as a quality failure of the audit.
testing.done: 15 cases carry an independent band re-derivation, and every auditor conclusion that accepted a wrong band or missing evidence is recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the derivative limit and authorisation checks
actions: Pick two month-ends and re-run the investment compliance rule set yourself, then compare the breach list to the one the auditor relied on.
Recompute single-counterparty exposure on the policy basis for the three largest counterparties and compare to the limit.
Match every derivative strategy traded in the sampled months to the permitted purposes in the derivatives use plan and confirm the plan version used was the one in force at the trade date.
Record as an exception any position the auditor passed that your re-run flags.
testing.done: re-run breach lists and recomputed counterparty exposures agree with the audit results, or the differences are recorded as exceptions.

testing.step: Trace tested controls to the underlying evidence and identifiers
actions: For each sampled control test, open the attribute sheet and confirm the evidence is attached rather than referenced by description.
Trace three sampled instances per control to their source identifiers — policy number, alert id, trade id, counterparty id — and confirm the identifiers exist in the source system.
Confirm the reviewer named on the evidence is a real, current employee and is not the performer.
Record any test supported only by an auditee assertion or a screenshot with no identifier as an evidence failure.
testing.done: every sampled control test has attached, identifier-traceable evidence with a segregated reviewer, or the gap is recorded.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline and threshold maths in the test results
actions: Recompute the suspicious activity reporting clock for every filed report in the sample against the applicable local deadline such as 30 calendar days from determination, and compare to the auditor conclusion.
Recompute the 30-day report issue clock and the 15-business-day management action clock for each sampled audit against the actual dates.
Recompute the 90-day retest window for every high finding closed in the year and identify retests performed late or on pre-fix instances.
Recompute the sample sizes used against the stated frequency-based rules and list any control tested on a sample smaller than the standard requires.
testing.done: reporting, issue, action and retest clocks are recomputed against actual dates and every undersized sample is listed.

testing.step: Trace remediation from finding to verified closure
actions: For every sampled closed finding, open the closure evidence and confirm it covers instances dated after the fix implementation date.
Confirm the closure was signed by the CAE for high and medium findings and not by the action owner.
Check reopened findings kept the original raise date so the ageing is not reset by the reopen.
List any finding closed on a management assertion alone as an exception, and re-rate any finding whose evidence shows the underlying control still fails.
testing.done: every sampled closure rests on post-fix evidence signed by the CAE, and assertion-only closures are listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the audit, the control or finding id, and whether the failure is in the first-line control or in the audit of it.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — coverage gap, insufficient sample, evidence not obtained, wrong rating, closure without retest, deferral without approval — and name a single owner.
Set a remediation date and mark whether the exception undermines reliance on the annual internal audit opinion.
Carry every open exception into next year quality review as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue record, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the quality review
actions: Compute the exception rate against sampled tests and against sampled closures and compare both to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — the annual key-control testing is reliable, reliable with exceptions, or not reliable — citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Internal Audit and performed none of the tests, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee alongside the internal audit opinion so the committee sees both, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the exception rates and a reliability conclusion, is reported to the Audit Committee and is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Board Governance Lead runs the independence and rotation file on behalf of the Audit Committee, which alone appoints, reappoints and removes the external auditor

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 8 Standard 8.3 and ICP 7 Standard 7.11 on independent oversight of the external audit, read against the current ICP text and cross-walked to the operative local rules: NAIC Model Audit Rule 205 Section 7 (five consecutive year lead and concurring partner limit, prohibited non-audit services, pre-approval) and Section 14 (audit committee independence), EU Audit Regulation 537/2014 (ten year firm rotation, seven year key partner rotation, seventy percent non-audit fee cap, prohibited services list) and the IESBA Code

In-scope processes.value: External audit engagement lifecycle for every audited entity in the group: annual appointment or reappointment, partner and firm tenure tracking, non-audit service pre-approval, fee monitoring, employment cooling-off checks and regulator notification of an auditor change

In-scope systems.value: Board portal holds the committee resolutions, independence letters and pre-approval decisions; the accounts payable ledger and the procurement system are the source of truth for what the audit firm was actually paid

Compliance procedure documented.value: External Auditor Independence and Rotation Procedure — engagement-level independence file, partner tenure register, prohibited service decision tree, pre-approval workflow with de minimis rules, fee ratio computation and the auditor change notification steps

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Audit Committee, not management, and reviewed annually and on any change to the Model Audit Rule, the EU Audit Regulation or the local ethical standard

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per engagement: independence and awareness letter obtained before the engagement letter is signed and the Model Audit Rule awareness letter filed with the domiciliary regulator by 31 December of the audited year; a change of auditor notified to the regulator within 5 business days and the reasons letter within 10 business days; the reappointment resolution passed before the engagement letter for the next year

Deadline reminders configured.value: Board portal calendar alerts the Board Governance Lead at 60 and 30 days before the 31 December awareness letter date, at 90 days before each partner reaches the fifth consecutive year, and at twelve months before the firm reaches an EU rotation cut-off

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Independence letters, partner tenure register, pre-approval decisions, fee analyses and committee resolutions retained 7 years from engagement end in the compliance evidence repository, indexed by audited entity, audit year and engagement partner

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any prohibited service performed, service started before pre-approval, partner over tenure or fee cap breach is logged as an independence exception with the impairment assessment, the remedial action and the disclosure decision

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs the impairment assessment and clears any decision that an independence breach does not require auditor replacement or regulator disclosure

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every external audit engagement in the group for the year, every engagement partner and concurring partner assigned to them, and every invoice paid to the audit firm and its network firms in the accounts payable ledger

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any prohibited non-audit service, any service started before pre-approval, any partner in a sixth consecutive year, or a non-audit to audit fee ratio above the applicable cap is a fail requiring an impairment assessment; a single fail is reported to the Audit Committee chair the same day

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per engagement; the test runs annually over all engagements for the year plus a quarterly fee and pre-approval sweep so a prohibited service is caught before the audit report is signed

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside the Corporate Secretariat and Finance and must not have prepared any pre-approval submission being tested

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual auditor independence test workpaper — engagement listing, tenure recomputation, fee analysis, pre-approval trace and exception log — in the compliance evidence repository under the audit year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Independence letters, awareness letter, partner tenure register, pre-approval log and fee analysis presentable to the domiciliary regulator or a financial condition examiner within 5 business days in Model Audit Rule Section 7 order

Regulator response path.value: Corporate Secretary responds to regulator questions on auditor qualification and change; General Counsel clears any admission of an independence breach before it is sent, and the Audit Committee chair approves the position taken

checklist.step: Open an independence file for each engagement before the engagement letter is signed
actions: Create one file per audited entity per audit year holding the entity name, regulator, audit year, proposed firm, engagement partner, concurring partner and proposed fee.
Record which rule set governs the engagement — Model Audit Rule Section 7, EU Audit Regulation 537/2014, the local ethical standard, or a combination for a group entity.
List the network firms of the proposed auditor that the group or its affiliates already buy services from, using the firm published network list.
Block the engagement letter from being signed until the file holds the firm independence confirmation and the tenure check result.
checklist.done: an engagement file exists per entity and year, names the governing rule set and the assigned partners, and no engagement letter is signed ahead of it.

checklist.step: Obtain the firm written independence confirmation and the awareness letter
actions: Request from the audit firm the annual independence confirmation addressed to the Audit Committee, listing all relationships between the firm, its network and the group that may bear on independence.

Request the Model Audit Rule awareness letter in which the firm states it is aware of and will conform to the applicable insurance statutes and regulations, and lodge it with the domiciliary regulator by 31 December of the audited year.
Check the confirmation covers the firm, the network firms and the individuals on the engagement team, not the signing partner alone.
Have the letters executed and filed to the engagement file with the received date recorded.
Reject a confirmation that omits the network firms and re-request rather than accepting a partial letter.
checklist.done: a signed independence confirmation covering firm, network and team, plus the awareness letter lodged by 31 December, are on the engagement file.

checklist.step: Recompute engagement and concurring partner tenure against the rotation limits
actions: Maintain a partner tenure register with one row per partner per entity per year, holding role, first year on the engagement and consecutive years served.

Count consecutive years including any year the partner served in a covered role for the entity, and apply the Model Audit Rule ceiling of five consecutive years for the lead and concurring partner with the five year cooling-off period.
For EU-scoped entities apply the seven year key audit partner limit with a three year cooling-off, and record whichever limit binds first for a dual-scope entity.
Alert the Audit Committee 90 days before any partner reaches the ceiling so a successor can be introduced with a handover year.
Record any regulator-granted relief from rotation with the relief letter attached, rather than assuming relief.
checklist.done: the tenure register shows recomputed consecutive years per partner and no partner is scheduled beyond the binding limit without an attached relief letter.

checklist.step: Track firm tenure and the mandatory retendering and rotation dates
actions: Record the first financial year the firm audited each entity and compute the consecutive years to date.

For EU public interest entities compute the ten year maximum engagement duration and the extensions available — up to twenty years with a public tender or twenty four with a joint audit — and record the date the current basis expires.
Set the retender milestone at least eighteen months before the expiry so the tender, committee recommendation and shareholder approval can complete in time.
Report firm tenure and the next mandatory rotation date to the Audit Committee annually in the reappointment paper.
checklist.done: firm tenure, the basis relied on for any extension and the next mandatory rotation date are recorded per entity and reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Screen every proposed service from the audit firm against the prohibited list
actions: Set a procurement block so no purchase requisition naming the audit firm or a network firm can be released without the independence screen.

Screen each proposed service against the prohibited categories: bookkeeping and accounting records, financial information systems design and implementation, appraisal and valuation, actuarial services contributing to the financial statements, internal audit outsourcing, management or human resources functions, broker-dealer or investment services, legal and expert services unrelated to the audit, and tax services on aggressive planning where the EU rules apply.
Record the service description, the category tested and the decision with the reasoning, and reject any request described only as advisory support.
Where a service is permissible, route it to the Audit Committee pre-approval workflow before any work starts.
Log any service found already started without pre-approval as an independence exception immediately.
checklist.done: every proposed audit-firm service has a documented category screen and either a pre-approval or a rejection recorded before work starts.

checklist.step: Run the Audit Committee pre-approval workflow
actions: Submit each permissible service to the committee with the scope, the fee estimate, the reason the audit firm is the appropriate provider and the safeguards applied.

Operate the de minimis exception only inside its stated conditions — the service was not recognised as non-audit at engagement, the aggregate is under the stated percentage of total fees paid, and it is approved before the audit completes — and record which condition was relied on.
Where authority is delegated to the committee chair between meetings, record the delegation resolution and report each chair approval to the full committee at its next sitting.
Capture the approval date and minute reference on the engagement file and pass the approved value to procurement as the purchase order ceiling.
checklist.done: each permissible service carries a dated committee or delegated chair approval with a minute reference, pre-dating the service start.

checklist.step: Compute the fee ratio and compare it to the applicable cap
actions: Extract from the accounts payable ledger every invoice paid in the year to the audit firm and its network firms across all group entities, using vendor id and parent vendor grouping rather than name search alone.
Classify each invoice as statutory audit, audit-related, tax or other non-audit service, agreeing the classification with the firm engagement listing.
Compute the non-audit to statutory audit fee ratio on a three consecutive financial year average for EU public interest entities and compare it to the seventy percent cap.
Reconcile the ledger total to the fee table disclosed in the financial statements and explain every difference.
Escalate a ratio approaching the cap to the Audit Committee before further non-audit services are approved.
checklist.done: the ledger-derived fee analysis reconciles to the disclosed fee table and the computed ratio is compared to the cap on the correct multi-year basis.

checklist.step: Check the employment and financial relationship restrictions
actions: Run a hire report for the year filtered to finance, actuarial and internal audit roles and match new joiners against the audit firm engagement team rosters for the prior two years.
Apply the cooling-off rule for a former engagement team member joining a financial reporting oversight role and record the last audit participation date and the elapsed period.
Confirm no officer, director or covered person holds a direct financial interest in the audit firm through the annual declarations of interest.
Check the engagement letter contains no indemnification or limitation of liability clause that would impair independence, and have General Counsel strike any that does.
checklist.done: no new hire in a financial reporting oversight role breaches the cooling-off period, declarations are complete, and the engagement letter carries no impairing clause.

checklist.step: Confirm the Audit Committee itself meets the independence requirement
actions: List the current committee members with their independence status determined against the stated criteria — no employment with the group or the auditor in the look-back period, no material business relationship, no compensation other than director fees.
Apply the Model Audit Rule Section 14 proportion required for the group direct written premium band and record the band and the resulting requirement.
Confirm at least one member has the financial or actuarial expertise the charter requires, naming the qualification relied on.
Record any member relying on an exemption or a hardship waiver with the waiver reference and its expiry.
checklist.done: committee composition is tested against the premium-band requirement with each member independence status and the financial expert named.

checklist.step: Assess the firm quality and inspection record before recommending appointment
actions: Read the firm most recent public audit regulator inspection report and its transparency report and note any findings on insurance or actuarial audits.
Ask the firm for the engagement quality review arrangements, the insurance specialist and actuarial specialist hours planned, and the group audit scoping including component auditor reliance.
Review the prior year audit performance: audit differences raised, late deliverables, restatements and the quality of the internal control communication.
Write a short assessment for the committee reappointment paper rather than presenting fees alone.
checklist.done: a written quality assessment covering inspection findings, specialist resourcing and prior year performance sits in the reappointment paper.

checklist.step: Pass the appointment or reappointment resolution
actions: Table the reappointment paper with the independence confirmation, the tenure position, the fee analysis and the quality assessment.
Have the Audit Committee resolve on appointment, remuneration and the terms of engagement, and minute that management did not determine the outcome.

Where shareholder approval is required, place the resolution on the general meeting agenda with the committee recommendation and, for EU entities, the two-option recommendation with a justified preference.
Record the resolution date and minute reference on the engagement file before the engagement letter is countersigned.
checklist.done: a minuted committee resolution on appointment, fee and terms pre-dates the countersigned engagement letter.

checklist.step: Handle an auditor change or resignation on the regulatory clock
actions: On any dismissal or resignation, notify the domiciliary regulator within 5 business days that the relationship has ended.

Within the following 10 business days file the letter stating whether there were any disagreements in the preceding twenty four months on accounting, auditing, or the scope of the audit, and their resolution.
Send the letter to the former auditor and obtain their written statement of agreement or disagreement, filing it with the regulator.
Notify every other regulator of a group entity the firm audits and update the engagement files and the tenure register.
checklist.done: the change notification is filed within 5 business days, the disagreements letter within 10, and the former auditor written response is on file.

checklist.step: Monitor independence continuously through the engagement
actions: Run a quarterly sweep of purchase orders and invoices naming the audit firm or a network firm and match each to a pre-approval record.
Ask the firm each quarter to confirm no new relationship has arisen, including network firm services bought by subsidiaries outside central procurement.
Re-run the fee ratio at each quarter with year-to-date figures so a breach is foreseen rather than discovered at year end.
Report the sweep result to the Audit Committee at every sitting, including a nil return.
checklist.done: each quarter shows a completed sweep, a firm confirmation, a refreshed fee ratio and a committee report, including nil returns.

checklist.step: Assess and dispose of any independence breach
actions: On any breach, document what the service or relationship was, when it started, who authorised it and the fee involved.
Assess impairment against the applicable rule — whether a reasonable and informed third party would conclude independence is compromised — and record the safeguards considered.
Decide and record the disposition: terminate the service and disclose, require the firm to remove the individual, or replace the auditor, and state why the chosen action is sufficient.
Report every breach and its disposition to the Audit Committee at the next sitting and to the regulator where the rule requires it.
checklist.done: each breach has a documented impairment assessment, a chosen disposition with reasoning, and committee and where required regulator reporting.

checklist.step: Retain the engagement independence file
actions: File the independence confirmation, awareness letter, tenure register extract, pre-approval decisions, fee analysis and committee resolutions per entity and audit year.
Apply the 7-years-from-engagement-end retention label and mark the file legal-hold-eligible.
Confirm the file is retrievable by audited entity, audit year, engagement partner name and audit firm.
Carry the closing tenure counts forward into next year register so the consecutive-year count never restarts by accident.
checklist.done: the engagement file is retained for 7 years, retrievable by entity, year and partner, with tenure counts carried forward.

testing.step: Build the population of engagements, partners and audit-firm payments
actions: List every audited entity in the group for the year with its auditor, engagement partner, concurring partner and audit fee from the engagement letters.

Extract every accounts payable invoice paid in the year to the audit firm and its network firms using the vendor parent grouping, not a name text match, and include entities outside central procurement.
Add the pre-approval log and the partner tenure register as the two control records to be tested against.
Reconcile the invoice population total to the fee table in the financial statements and resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: the engagement, partner and payment populations are extracted and the payment total reconciles to the disclosed fee table.

testing.step: Reconcile every audit-firm payment to a pre-approval that pre-dates it
actions: Match each non-audit invoice to a pre-approval record on service description, entity and value.
Compare the approval date to the earliest service delivery date on the invoice or statement of work and flag every service that started first.
List unmatched invoices as automatic exceptions with no judgement applied.
Check any de minimis reliance names the specific condition relied on and that the aggregate stayed inside the stated percentage.
testing.done: every non-audit payment matches a pre-approval dated before service start, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100 percent of engagement and concurring partners and 100 percent of non-audit services above the de minimis value.
Take a seeded random sample of 20 invoices from the remaining audit-firm payment population.
Take 100 percent of entities where the firm has audited for more than eight consecutive years.
Record the seed, population sizes, sample sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample covers all partners, all above-de-minimis services and all long-tenure firms, and is reproducible from the recorded seed.

testing.step: Recompute partner and firm tenure independently
actions: Rebuild consecutive years served for each sampled partner from the signed audit reports and the firm engagement letters rather than from the tenure register.

Compare your count to the register and to the binding limit — five consecutive years under Model Audit Rule Section 7, seven under the EU key audit partner rule — and identify anyone in an over-run year.
Recompute the cooling-off period served by any returning partner and check it met the full five or three year requirement.
Rebuild firm tenure per entity from the earliest signed report and compare to the ten year EU maximum and any extension basis claimed.
testing.done: partner and firm tenure are rebuilt from signed reports, compared to the binding limits, and any over-run or short cooling-off is identified.

testing.step: Re-perform the prohibited service classification
actions: Open the statement of work behind each sampled non-audit service and read what was actually delivered rather than the invoice narrative.
Classify the work yourself against the prohibited categories before reading the recorded screen decision.
Pay specific attention to services described as accounting advisory, model validation, actuarial support and systems implementation, which most often sit on the prohibited line.
Record any difference between your classification and the recorded one as an exception, including a right answer supported by no reasoning.
testing.done: each sampled service has an independent classification derived from the statement of work, with differences from the recorded screen listed.

testing.step: Recompute the fee ratio and its multi-year basis
actions: Rebuild the audit and non-audit fee split from the invoice population using your own classification results, not the recorded one.
Recompute the non-audit to statutory audit ratio on the three consecutive financial year average for EU public interest entities and on a single year basis for the remaining entities.
Compare the recomputed ratio to the seventy percent cap and identify the year in which any breach first arose.
Reconcile your rebuilt split to the disclosed fee table and explain every difference above the disclosure rounding.
testing.done: the fee ratio is recomputed from an independently classified invoice population on the correct multi-year basis and reconciled to the disclosure.

testing.step: Trace appointment and independence evidence to the committee minutes
actions: For each sampled engagement, find the resolution on appointment, remuneration and terms in the minutes and confirm it pre-dates the countersigned engagement letter.
Confirm the independence confirmation on file covers the firm, network firms and the engagement team and carries a date inside the engagement year.
Confirm the awareness letter was lodged with the domiciliary regulator by 31 December and capture the lodgement acknowledgement.
Check that every chair-delegated approval was reported back to the full committee at the following sitting.
testing.done: each sampled engagement traces to a dated minute, a full-scope independence confirmation and a timely awareness letter lodgement.

testing.step: Test the committee independence and the employment cooling-off checks
actions: Re-derive each committee member independence status from the declarations of interest and the related party register rather than accepting the recorded status.
Recompute the required independent proportion from the group direct written premium band and compare it to the actual composition.
Re-run the new hire match against the audit firm engagement rosters for finance, actuarial and internal audit roles and recompute the elapsed cooling-off period for any match.
Flag any member relying on a waiver whose expiry has passed.
testing.done: committee composition and hire cooling-off are independently recomputed against the premium band and the roster match, with expired waivers flagged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the entity, audit year, partner or service, and the rule breached.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — service bought outside central procurement, screen not run, approval after start, tenure miscounted, fee classification wrong, waiver lapsed — and name a single owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any prohibited service or partner over-run, open an impairment assessment with General Counsel the same day.
Carry every open exception into next year test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a date and, where the rule was breached, an opened impairment assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the independence test
actions: Count the fails against the zero-tolerance threshold and state the number of prohibited services, late pre-approvals, tenure over-runs and cap breaches found.
Write the conclusion — auditor independence maintained, maintained with exceptions, or impaired — with the workpaper references behind each fail.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside the Corporate Secretariat and Finance and prepared none of the tested submissions, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee before the audit report is signed and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the fail counts and an independence conclusion, is reported to the committee before the audit report is signed, and is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Controller owns preparation and lodgement of the audited financial report and the auditor communications; the Chief Financial Officer signs and the Audit Committee approves before filing

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 8 Standards 8.3 and 8.8 and ICP 7 Standard 7.11 on external audit and board oversight, read against the current ICP text and cross-walked to the operative filing rules: NAIC Model Audit Rule 205 Sections 4, 11, 12 and 16 (1 June audited report, 1 August internal control communication and management report, 5 business day adverse condition notice) and Solvency II Articles 51 and 256 with the 14 and 20 week SFCR clocks

In-scope processes.value: Year-end external audit and statutory filing cycle for every audited legal entity: statutory and IFRS statement preparation, audit support, audit difference resolution, opinion receipt, board approval, lodgement with each domiciliary and group supervisor, and the auditor internal control communication

In-scope systems.value: Statutory statement preparation and electronic lodgement to the NAIC and each state; the consolidation tool produces the IFRS group figures and the financial reporting repository holds the filed sets and receipts

Compliance procedure documented.value: Audited Financial Report Filing Procedure — jurisdiction deliverable calendar, audit timetable and request management, audit difference and unadjusted differences protocol, representation letter, approval route and per-jurisdiction lodgement steps with receipt capture

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and reviewed by the Audit Committee each year before the audit starts; changes to a filing deadline or channel require a documented update before the next cycle

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Audited financial report to the domiciliary commissioner by 1 June following 31 December year end, with any extension request lodged at least 10 days before that date; auditor communication of internal control related matters and the management report on internal control by 1 August; adverse financial condition or material misstatement notice within 5 business days of the auditor determination; Solvency II SFCR at 14 weeks solo and 20 weeks group after year end

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar alerts the Controller at 60, 30 and 10 days before each 1 June and 1 August date per entity, opens the extension decision task at 25 days before 1 June, and pages the CFO on the day any lodgement receipt is still outstanding

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Filed audited financial reports, opinions, representation letters, internal control communications, board approvals and every lodgement receipt retained 7 years from filing in the financial reporting repository, indexed by entity, year and jurisdiction

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A late lodgement, a missing jurisdiction, a filing without board approval or a rejected submission is logged with the days late, the regulator contacted, the corrective filing date and the root cause

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs off every late or corrected filing and any decision not to notify a regulator of a matter the auditor raised

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on completeness and timeliness — any jurisdiction not filed, any filing after its statutory date without an approved extension, any filing lodged before board approval, and any auditor-identified adverse condition not notified within 5 business days is a fail reported to the Audit Committee chair the same day
