checklist.step: Build the audited-statement deliverable calendar for every entity and jurisdiction
actions: List every audited legal entity with its domicile, all states or countries of licensure, its group supervisor and its financial year end.

For each entity load the deliverables and their statutory dates: audited financial report by 1 June, auditor internal control communication and management report by 1 August, awareness letter by 31 December, plus the SFCR at 14 weeks and the group SFCR at 20 weeks where Solvency II applies.

Record the lodgement channel per jurisdiction — electronic filing to the NAIC and the state department, the supervisor portal, or a paper or email lodgement address — with the account and credentials owner named.
Read each state annual statement filing checklist for the current year and note any jurisdiction that requires the audited report in hard copy or with a specific transmittal.
Publish the calendar to Finance, Actuarial and the Corporate Secretary with the owner named on every line.
checklist.done: every entity and jurisdiction has a dated deliverable line with a channel, an owner and a current-year filing checklist reference.

checklist.step: Agree the audit timetable and deliverable list with the firm
actions: Hold the audit planning meeting and agree the interim and final fieldwork dates, the group audit scoping and which components receive full-scope audits.
Back-schedule from 1 June: opinion date, board approval date, representation letter date, final clearance, fieldwork end and the request list issue date.
Agree the specialist involvement in writing — actuarial specialists on policy liabilities, valuation specialists on level 3 investments — and the dates their work must complete.
Confirm the firm will issue the internal control communication in time for the 1 August lodgement rather than at its own convenience.
Circulate the agreed timetable and have each internal owner accept their dates.
checklist.done: a back-scheduled timetable from 1 June is agreed in writing with the firm, including specialist dates and the internal control communication date.

checklist.step: Prepare the statutory financial statements and tie them to the ledger
actions: Load the final trial balance into the statement preparation software and complete the pages in order: Jurat, Assets, Liabilities Surplus and Other Funds, Summary of Operations, Cash Flow and the supporting exhibits and schedules.

Tie Exhibit 5 and Exhibit 6 reserve totals to the actuarial valuation output, Schedule S to the ceded reinsurance records, Schedule D to the investment book of record and Schedule F to the reinsurance recoverable analysis.
Clear every cross-check and validation the software reports and document the reason for any that is overridden.
Reconcile the statutory surplus to the GAAP or IFRS equity through the documented bridge and have a second preparer review the bridge.
Freeze the statement version that goes to audit and record the version id.
checklist.done: all statement pages tie to the source records, every validation is cleared or documented, and the audited version is frozen with a version id.

checklist.step: Prepare the notes, disclosures and the basis-of-accounting reconciliation
actions: Draft the notes to the financial statements against the current disclosure checklist, covering permitted or prescribed accounting practices, related party transactions, reinsurance risk transfer, capital and surplus requirements and subsequent events.
Quantify any permitted or prescribed practice and its effect on surplus and risk-based capital, since the regulator reads this before anything else.
Prepare the IFRS 17 disclosures for the group accounts including the contractual service margin roll-forward and the risk adjustment confidence level.
Have the disclosure checklist signed by the preparer and a reviewer, with each item marked complete, not applicable with a reason, or outstanding.
checklist.done: notes are complete against a signed disclosure checklist and every permitted or prescribed practice is quantified with its surplus and capital effect.

checklist.step: Run audit support and the request list to a controlled close
actions: Publish the request list to a shared audit workspace with an owner and a due date on every line and no requests routed through personal email.
Deliver each item as a reproducible extract with the source system, extract date, filter criteria and record count on the cover, not as a hand-built spreadsheet.
Track ageing daily and escalate any item more than 3 business days overdue to the process owner manager.
Log every item the auditor rejects or re-requests with the reason so the same defect is not repeated next cycle.
checklist.done: every request is delivered with a reproducible extract cover, the ageing is nil at fieldwork end and rejections are logged with reasons.

checklist.step: Resolve audit differences and record the unadjusted ones
actions: Maintain the schedule of audit differences with the account, the amount, the effect on surplus and income, and whether it is factual, judgemental or projected.
Post every difference the company accepts before the statement version is refrozen and re-run the affected cross-checks.
For each unadjusted difference record the reason it is not posted and compare the aggregate to performance materiality and to the risk-based capital effect.
Take the schedule of unadjusted differences to the Audit Committee with the aggregate effect on surplus stated in figures, not in words.
checklist.done: differences are posted or listed with reasons, and the unadjusted aggregate with its surplus and capital effect is before the committee.

checklist.step: Obtain the opinion and check its form before relying on it
actions: Receive the draft auditor report and check the addressee, the entity name, the financial year, the basis of accounting described and the date.
Check the opinion type and read any modification, emphasis of matter, going concern paragraph or key audit matter, and confirm every one is consistent with the disclosures filed.
Confirm the report describes the statutory basis as the applicable framework where the filing is statutory, since an opinion on the wrong framework does not satisfy the filing requirement.
Confirm the signing partner is the partner recorded in the independence file and is within the rotation limits.
Do not release the statements until the opinion is dated on or after the board approval and the representation letter.
checklist.done: the opinion names the right entity, year, framework and partner, and its date is on or after board approval and the representation letter.

checklist.step: Prepare and sign the management representation letter
actions: Review the letter for the standard representations plus the insurer-specific ones — completeness of reinsurance contracts and side agreements, risk transfer conclusions, actuarial assumption responsibility, and unrecorded liabilities.
Confirm each factual representation with the named owner in Finance, Actuarial, Legal and Reinsurance before signing, and record their confirmations.
Confirm the disclosure of all known instances of fraud, non-compliance and regulatory correspondence, checking the legal and compliance registers rather than relying on recall.
Sign with the CEO and date the letter no earlier than the opinion date, and file the signed copy to the engagement folder.
checklist.done: a CEO and CFO signed letter, dated no earlier than the opinion, is on file with each factual representation confirmed by its named owner.

checklist.step: Take the statements and the auditor report to the Audit Committee and the board
actions: Circulate the audited statements, the opinion, the unadjusted differences schedule and the auditor internal control communication draft through the board portal at least 5 business days before the meeting.
Schedule the auditor private session with the committee without management present and record that it happened.
Minute the committee recommendation and the board approval of the statements, capturing the resolution wording and the date.
Release the statements for filing only after the approval resolution is recorded.
checklist.done: board approval of the statements is minuted with a date, an auditor private session is recorded, and no filing left before that date.

checklist.step: Lodge the audited financial report by 1 June in every jurisdiction
actions: Submit the audited financial report electronically to the NAIC and to the domiciliary department, plus every other state that requires a copy, working the calendar line by line.
Attach the required transmittal or cover letter per state and pay any filing fee through the prescribed channel.
Capture the confirmation number, timestamp and receipt for each lodgement and attach it to the calendar line, treating an unconfirmed submission as not filed.
Chase any jurisdiction that has not acknowledged within 2 business days of submission and record the contact.
Mark the calendar line complete only when the receipt is attached.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction line shows a submission with a captured confirmation number and receipt dated on or before 1 June.

checklist.step: File the auditor internal control communication and the management report by 1 August
actions: Obtain from the auditor the written communication of internal control related matters noted in the audit, covering every unremediated material weakness.
Prepare management written response describing the remediation for each matter with an owner and a date, and reconcile the matters to the internal deficiency log so nothing is omitted.
Lodge the communication and, where the premium threshold requires it, the management report on internal control over financial reporting with the domiciliary commissioner by 1 August.
Capture the lodgement receipt and file both documents to the reporting year folder.
checklist.done: the auditor communication and management response, reconciled to the deficiency log, are lodged by 1 August with receipts captured.

checklist.step: Handle extensions, exemptions and the 5 business day adverse condition notice
actions: Where a 1 June date cannot be met, request the extension in writing from the commissioner at least 10 days before the date, stating the reason and the proposed filing date, and file the approval when it comes back.
Track any exemption or hardship relief granted to a small entity, with the granting letter, its conditions and its expiry recorded on the calendar line.

If the auditor determines the insurer does not meet its minimum capital and surplus requirement or identifies a material misstatement, notify the commissioner within 5 business days of that determination and record the notification date and recipient.
Escalate any of these events to the CFO, General Counsel and the Audit Committee chair on the day it arises.
checklist.done: extensions are requested at least 10 days ahead with approvals on file, and any adverse determination is notified within 5 business days with the record kept.

checklist.step: File the audited solvency and group returns on their own clocks
actions: Prepare the Solvency and Financial Condition Report with the audited solvency balance sheet and lodge it at 14 weeks after year end for solo entities and 20 weeks for the group, through the supervisor portal.
Prepare and lodge the annual quantitative reporting templates that carry audit assurance, checking each passes the supervisor validation rule set before submission.
For other jurisdictions lodge the audited annual return on its own statutory date through its own channel and record the acknowledgement.
Reconcile the audited figures in every solvency return back to the audited financial statements and document each reconciling item.
checklist.done: every audited solvency and group return is lodged on its own deadline with validations passed and a reconciliation to the audited statements.

checklist.step: Track receipts, regulator queries and post-filing corrections
actions: Reconcile the calendar to receipts at 1 June plus 3 business days and again at 1 August plus 3 business days and open an exception for any line without a receipt.
Log every regulator query on a filing with the date received, the response due date and the owner, and answer inside the stated window.
Where a correction or refiling is needed, prepare an amended filing with a cover letter explaining what changed and why, and obtain CFO sign-off before lodging.
Record the days late and the root cause for any deliverable that missed its date.
checklist.done: the calendar is reconciled to receipts after each deadline, every query has a dated response, and each correction carries a CFO-approved cover letter.

checklist.step: Retain the filed set and close the reporting year
actions: File per entity and year the audited statements as filed, the opinion, the representation letter, the unadjusted differences schedule, the internal control communication, the management report, the board approval minute and every receipt.
Apply the 7-years-from-filing retention label and mark the set legal-hold-eligible.
Confirm the set is retrievable by legal entity, reporting year, jurisdiction and deliverable type.
Record the closing position of the calendar — filed, extended, exempt — against every line so next year opens from a known state.
checklist.done: the complete filed set per entity and jurisdiction is retained for 7 years, retrievable, with every calendar line closed to a known status.

testing.step: Build the population of audited-statement deliverables due in the year
actions: Rebuild the entity and jurisdiction list from the corporate registry and the licence register rather than from the filing calendar, so a missing calendar line is visible.

Derive the deliverables owed per entity from the applicable rules — 1 June audited report, 1 August internal control communication and management report, SFCR at 14 and 20 weeks — and compare to the calendar.
Add every extension request and exemption claimed in the year.
Sign the population as complete, recording the registry extract date and record counts.
testing.done: the deliverable population is rebuilt from the licence register and reconciled to the filing calendar, with every difference listed.

testing.step: Reconcile every deliverable to a lodgement receipt
actions: Match each population line to a receipt or confirmation number in the repository and open the receipt rather than relying on the calendar status flag.
Compare the receipt timestamp to the statutory date and compute the days early or late for every line.
List every line with no receipt, a receipt for the wrong entity or year, or a receipt that post-dates the deadline without an approved extension as an automatic exception.
Check each claimed extension has the written commissioner approval attached and that the request itself was made at least 10 days before the original date.
testing.done: every deliverable traces to an opened receipt with a computed days-late figure, and unsupported extensions are listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100 percent of entities whose filing was late, extended, amended or subject to a regulator query.
Take a seeded random sample of 8 remaining entity-jurisdiction lines across at least three different lodgement channels.
Take 100 percent of internal control communications and management reports.
Record the seed, population size, sample size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers all late, extended and amended filings plus a reproducible random selection across multiple channels.

testing.step: Re-perform the filed-content check against the board-approved statements
actions: Retrieve the filed document from the regulator system or the lodgement receipt package for each sampled line, not the internal working copy.
Compare the filed statement page by page to the board-approved version and identify any figure or note that differs.
Check the auditor opinion attached names the correct entity, year and reporting framework and is signed by the partner in the independence file.
Confirm the filed version post-dates the board approval minute and the representation letter.
testing.done: each sampled filed document is confirmed identical to the board-approved version with a correctly scoped, correctly signed opinion attached.

testing.step: Trace statement figures back to the ledger and the actuarial output
actions: For each sampled entity tie total assets, total liabilities and surplus in the filed statement to the final audited trial balance.
Tie the Exhibit 5 and Exhibit 6 reserve totals to the actuarial valuation output and the model run id the Appointed Actuary certified.
Tie Schedule F reinsurance recoverables to the ceded records and Schedule D to the investment book of record.
List any tie-out difference with its amount and whether it changes surplus or risk-based capital.
testing.done: surplus, reserves, reinsurance and investment totals in the filed statements tie to the ledger and the certified valuation output, or differences are quantified.

testing.step: Test the auditor communication and management report content
actions: Read the auditor internal control communication and list every matter raised with its severity as the auditor stated it.
Match each matter to a deficiency record in the internal log and flag any matter the company never logged.
Confirm the management report on internal control discloses every unremediated material weakness and that its conclusion agrees with the internal assessment.
Check the response to each matter names a fix, an owner and a date rather than a general commitment.
testing.done: every auditor-raised matter matches a logged deficiency with an owned, dated response and the management report omits no unremediated material weakness.

testing.step: Recompute every statutory deadline and notification clock
actions: Recompute each entity 1 June and 1 August dates from its financial year end rather than assuming a December year end.
Recompute the Solvency II 14 week solo and 20 week group dates from year end and compare to the actual submission timestamps.
Recompute the 10 day lead requirement on every extension request and the 5 business day clock on any adverse condition notification, using business days and the applicable jurisdiction holidays.
List every clock missed with the number of days and whether the miss was self-identified or found by the regulator.
testing.done: all filing, extension and notification clocks are recomputed from entity-specific year ends and every miss is quantified in days.

testing.step: Test that no filing preceded its approval and no query went unanswered
actions: For each sampled filing compare the lodgement timestamp to the board approval minute timestamp and treat any filing that came first as a fail regardless of content accuracy.
Trace every regulator query in the tracker to a dated response and confirm the response left inside the window the regulator set.
For each amended filing confirm a CFO-approved cover letter explaining the change accompanied it.
Confirm the auditor private session with the committee took place before the statements were approved.
testing.done: no sampled filing pre-dates its approval, every query has an in-window dated response and each amendment carries a CFO-approved explanation.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the entity, jurisdiction, deliverable and the days late or the content defect.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — jurisdiction missing from the calendar, receipt never captured, approval after filing, audit timetable slipped, extension requested late, notification clock missed — and name a single owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any missed regulator notification, open a self-report assessment with General Counsel the same day.
Carry every open exception into next year test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a date and, where a notification was missed, an opened self-report assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the filing test
actions: State the counts: deliverables due, filed on time, filed late with days, filed under approved extension, and not filed.
Write the conclusion — filing obligations met, met with exceptions, or not met — with the workpaper references behind each fail.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared and lodged none of the tested filings and sits outside the Controller organisation, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the due, on-time, late and unfiled counts with a stated conclusion, reported to the committee and filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Appointed Actuary owns the reserve figure certified to the regulator; the Valuation Actuary owns the production runs and the Chief Actuary owns the assumption governance behind them

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 8 Standards 8.3 and 8.8 on the actuarial control function read against the current ICP text, and cross-walked to the valuation standards actually applied: NAIC Valuation Manual VM-20 and VM-21 principle-based reserves with VM-31 documentation, IFRS 17 fulfilment cash flows, risk adjustment and contractual service margin, and the Solvency II Article 77 best estimate plus risk margin at the six percent cost of capital

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly and annual policy liability valuation for every in-force segment: seriatim data extract and reconciliation, assumption setting and approval, model run execution, reserve computation on each prescribed basis, movement analysis, reserve posting to the ledger and the actuarial report documentation

In-scope systems.value: Valuation models and run controls, fed by the policy administration in-force extract and the investment book of record; assumption sets and model versions are held in the model governance repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Policy Liability Valuation Procedure — data extract and reconciliation standard, assumption change governance, model version control, run log and reproducibility rules, reserve computation by basis, movement analysis and the reserve posting and certification steps

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and reviewed by the board risk committee annually; every methodology change needs Chief Actuary approval before the run and disclosure in the actuarial report

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly valuation closes on working day 8 for the quarterly statement due 15 May, 15 August and 15 November; the annual valuation supports the annual statement due 1 March and the VM-31 principle-based reserving actuarial report due 1 April; the Solvency II annual technical provisions feed the quantitative templates at 14 weeks after year end

Deadline reminders configured.value: Valuation calendar tasks open the data extract on working day 2 and alert the Valuation Actuary at 3 and 1 days before each run gate — data lock, assumption lock, run complete, review complete, post to ledger — escalating a missed gate to the Chief Actuary the same day

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Data reconciliations, assumption approval records, model version and run ids, model output, movement analyses and reviewer sign-offs retained 7 years from the valuation date in the model governance repository, indexed by valuation date, segment and basis

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Data reconciliation breaks above tolerance, unapproved assumption changes, runs on unvalidated model versions and post-close reserve adjustments are logged with the reserve amount affected, the cause and the correction

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Actuary signs off every methodology or assumption correction and every post-close reserve adjustment before it reaches the ledger

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every valuation segment and reserve basis produced at each quarterly and annual valuation date, together with the seriatim in-force records feeding them and the reserve journals posted to the ledger

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Data reconciliation must agree within 0.1 percent of policy count and face amount with every break explained; a reserve that cannot be reproduced from the recorded model version, assumption set and input data is a fail; any assumption change applied without prior approval is a fail regardless of its reserve effect

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation runs quarterly and annually; the test runs quarterly on data reconciliation and run controls and annually in full including reproduction of the year-end reserve and the movement analysis

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside the valuation production team and must not have built, calibrated or run any model being tested

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly and annual valuation control test workpaper — reconciliation results, reproduced run comparison, assumption approval trace and exception log — in the model governance repository cross-referenced from the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: VM-31 actuarial report, assumption and methodology documentation, data reconciliations and the model validation reports, producible for a domiciliary examination, an NAIC principle-based reserving review or a group-wide supervisor request within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Appointed Actuary answers valuation methodology and assumption questions with the Chief Actuary informed; the CFO clears any communication that would change a filed reserve figure and the board risk committee chair is told of any restatement

checklist.step: Open the valuation cycle and lock the calendar gates
actions: Open the valuation cycle for the quarter or year end with the five gates dated: data lock, assumption lock, run complete, review complete, post to ledger.
Back-schedule the gates from the ledger posting date needed for the statement deadline — 15 May, 15 August and 15 November for quarters and 1 March for the annual statement.
Confirm with the Controller the working day the reserve journal must land so the close is not held.
List the segments and bases to be produced this cycle: statutory formulaic, VM-20 and VM-21 principle-based, IFRS 17 and the Solvency II best estimate and risk margin.
Publish the cycle plan to Actuarial, Finance and Data Engineering with owners on every gate.
checklist.done: the cycle plan carries five dated gates back-scheduled from the statement deadline, with every segment and basis listed and owned.

checklist.step: Extract the seriatim in-force and reconcile it to the policy administration
actions: Run the valuation extract as at the valuation date, taking one record per policy or per coverage segment with issue date, plan code, face amount, account value, premium mode, rider set and status.

Reconcile extract policy counts, face amount, account value and annualised premium to the policy administration control totals and to the prior valuation roll-forward of new business, terminations and reinstatements.
Explain every break above the 0.1 percent tolerance to a named cause — timing, a status change after cut-off, a plan code newly added — and do not proceed on an unexplained break.
Run the data quality rule set for missing issue ages, impossible dates, negative account values and unmapped plan codes, and clear or quarantine every hit.
Sign the data reconciliation and attach it to the cycle before the data lock gate closes.
checklist.done: counts, face amount and account value reconcile within 0.1 percent with every break explained, the rule set is clear, and the reconciliation is signed before data lock.

checklist.step: Refresh and approve the assumption set
actions: Review the experience studies supporting mortality, lapse, premium persistency, partial withdrawal, annuitisation and expense assumptions, checking each study credibility and its exposure period.
For each proposed change record the current assumption, the proposed assumption, the experience basis, the credibility weighting and the estimated reserve impact before it is applied.

Set the prescribed elements separately from the company elements — VM-20 prescribed mortality tables and margins, the Solvency II risk-free curve with any volatility adjustment, the IFRS 17 discount rate approach — and record the published version used.
Approve or reject each change in writing and freeze the assumption set with a version id at the assumption lock gate.
Reject any change proposed after assumption lock into the next cycle unless it corrects an error, and document that decision.
checklist.done: every assumption change carries an experience basis and an estimated impact, is approved in writing, and the set is frozen with a version id at assumption lock.

checklist.step: Confirm the model version is validated and fit for the run
actions: Check the model version scheduled for the run carries a current validation with no open high-severity validation finding.
Confirm every code change since the last valuation has a change ticket, a test result and an impact analysis showing the reserve effect in isolation.
Confirm the model inventory entry names the model owner, the validator, the last validation date and the next due date.
Block the run on any model whose validation has lapsed and escalate to the Chief Actuary rather than proceeding with a caveat.
checklist.done: the scheduled model version has a current validation, no open high findings, and every code change since last valuation carries a tested, impact-assessed ticket.

checklist.step: Execute the valuation runs and capture the run identifiers
actions: Launch each production run naming the input data version, assumption set version, model version and economic scenario set, and record the run id the platform issues.

For principle-based reserves run the deterministic reserve, the stochastic reserve over the prescribed scenario set and the net premium reserve, and record the result of the exclusion tests where they were applied.
Check run completion diagnostics — projection convergence, scenario count, policies dropped, negative reserve cells — and investigate every dropped policy rather than netting it off.
Store the outputs, logs and diagnostics against the run id so the reserve can be reproduced from the four recorded versions alone.
Do not re-run without a new run id, so no output can quietly overwrite the one under review.
checklist.done: every reserve figure has a run id tied to a named data, assumption, model and scenario version, with diagnostics stored and no dropped policy unexplained.

checklist.step: Compute the reserve on each prescribed basis
actions: For statutory principle-based segments take the reserve as the greatest of the net premium reserve, the deterministic reserve and the stochastic reserve at the model segment level, and document the binding component.
For formulaic segments compute the reserve on the prescribed table, interest rate and method for the issue year and record the valuation basis per plan code.
For IFRS 17 build the fulfilment cash flows, the risk adjustment at the disclosed confidence level and the contractual service margin roll-forward with the coverage units used.

For Solvency II compute the best estimate discounted on the published risk-free curve and add the risk margin at the six percent cost of capital, showing the projected solvency capital requirement run-off.
Reconcile the bases to each other through a documented bridge so the difference between statutory, IFRS and solvency reserves is explained rather than merely observed.
checklist.done: each basis is computed on its own prescribed method with the binding component documented, and the bases reconcile through a written bridge.

checklist.step: Produce the movement analysis and challenge the drivers
actions: Build the reserve walk from prior valuation to current, splitting the movement into new business, expected release, actual versus expected experience, assumption changes, methodology changes, model changes and economic movement.
Tie the assumption change component back to the estimated impacts recorded at approval and explain differences above the stated tolerance.
Isolate the model change component by running the current data and assumptions through the prior model version, so a code effect cannot hide inside experience.
Present unexplained residual as its own line and refuse to close the cycle with a residual above the tolerance.
checklist.done: the reserve walk splits every component including an isolated model change effect, and the unexplained residual is inside tolerance.

checklist.step: Run the independent second-actuary review
actions: Re-perform the reserve calculation for a set of sample policies by hand or in an independent spreadsheet and compare cell by cell to the model output.
Check the reserve per unit of face amount and per policy against the prior period and against a benchmark for that plan and issue-year cohort, investigating outliers.
Test the exclusion test results and the binding-component conclusion independently on at least two segments.
Record the review findings, the disposition of each and the reviewer name and date on the cycle record.
checklist.done: sample policy recalculations, ratio checks and exclusion test conclusions are independently reproduced with findings dispositioned and signed.

checklist.step: Post the reserve to the ledger with a traceable reference
actions: Receive the certified reserve schedule by segment and basis from the Appointed Actuary with the run ids on it.
Post the reserve journal with the run id and valuation date in the journal reference so the ledger balance links to a reproducible run.
Reconcile the posted balance to the actuarial schedule and to the Exhibit 5 and Exhibit 6 totals in the statement, and clear any difference before close.
Route the journal for approval by a preparer-independent approver and retain the approval evidence.
checklist.done: the ledger reserve equals the certified actuarial schedule, carries the run id in its reference, and was approved by someone other than the preparer.

checklist.step: Reconcile reserves to the reinsurance ceded position
actions: Compute the ceded reserve on the same basis as the gross reserve using the treaty terms in force at the valuation date.
Reconcile ceded reserves and reserve credit to the reinsurance administration records and to Schedule S, explaining every difference.
Confirm reserve credit is only taken where the reinsurer is authorised or the collateral required by the credit for reinsurance rules is in place, and record the collateral amount and form.
Flag any treaty whose risk transfer conclusion has changed so the gross and net presentation follows it.
checklist.done: ceded reserves tie to the reinsurance records and Schedule S, and every reserve credit is supported by authorised status or recorded collateral.

checklist.step: Document the valuation in the actuarial report
actions: Write the VM-31 principle-based reserving actuarial report covering the model description, the assumptions with their support, the margins, the exclusion tests, the sensitivities and the reliance on others, for filing by 1 April.
Document the IFRS 17 methodology choices — measurement model, transition approach, discount rate derivation, risk adjustment technique and confidence level, and the coverage unit definition.
State every material judgement and every change from the prior valuation with its reserve effect, since an undisclosed change is the finding examiners raise most.
Attach the data reconciliations, assumption approvals, run ids and the movement analysis as the report exhibits.
checklist.done: an actuarial report is complete with methodology, assumptions, judgements, changes and the supporting exhibits, ready for the 1 April filing.

checklist.step: Take the valuation results to the board risk committee
actions: Present the reserve level by basis, the movement analysis, the assumption changes made and their impact, and the areas of greatest estimation uncertainty.
State the actuarial function opinion on the adequacy of technical provisions, on pricing adequacy and on reinsurance, as the actuarial control function is expected to report.
Flag any segment where experience is diverging from assumption and state what will change next cycle.
Record the committee minute reference against the valuation cycle.
checklist.done: the committee has received reserves by basis, the movement, assumption impacts and the actuarial function opinion, with a minute reference recorded.

checklist.step: Control post-close adjustments and restatements
actions: Log any reserve error found after the cycle closes with the amount, the affected segment, the valuation dates involved and the cause.
Assess materiality against surplus and risk-based capital and decide between correcting in the current period and restating the prior filing, recording the reasoning.
Obtain Chief Actuary and CFO approval before any post-close adjustment reaches the ledger, and inform the Appointed Actuary where a certified figure moves.
Raise a model or process fix so the same error cannot recur, with an owner and a date.
checklist.done: each post-close error has a quantified materiality assessment, an approved correction route, and a preventive fix with an owner.

checklist.step: Feed experience back into the next assumption cycle
actions: Load actual mortality, lapse, withdrawal and expense experience for the period into the experience warehouse with exposure measured consistently with the assumption basis.
Compute actual to expected ratios by product, issue year and duration band and flag any cell breaching the monitoring threshold.
Prepare the experience study updates required for the statutory experience reporting submission and for the next assumption review.
Hand the flagged cells to the Chief Actuary as the agenda for the next assumption lock.
checklist.done: actual to expected ratios are computed by product, issue year and duration, and breaching cells are on the next assumption review agenda.

checklist.step: Archive the valuation cycle evidence
actions: Archive per valuation date the input data snapshot, assumption set version, model version, run ids, outputs, diagnostics, reconciliations, review notes and the certified schedule.
Apply the 7-years-from-valuation-date retention label and mark the archive legal-hold-eligible.
Confirm the archive supports reproduction — that a reviewer can restore the data and assumption versions and re-run the model to the same reserve.
Index the archive by valuation date, segment, basis and run id.
checklist.done: each valuation date is archived in a reproducible form, labelled for 7-year retention and indexed by segment, basis and run id.

testing.step: Build the population of valuation segments, runs and reserve journals
actions: Extract every valuation segment and basis produced at each valuation date in the year with its run id, data version, assumption version and model version.
Extract every reserve journal posted to the ledger in the year with its valuation date and reference.
Add the seriatim in-force record counts per valuation date from the extract logs.
Reconcile the run population to the journal population and list any reserve posted with no corresponding run id.
testing.done: runs, segments and reserve journals are extracted and reconciled, with any journal lacking a run id listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the valuation in-force to the policy administration source of record
actions: Pull the policy administration control totals at each valuation date independently and compare policy count, face amount, account value and annualised premium to the valuation extract.
Recompute the variance percentage against the 0.1 percent tolerance rather than accepting the reconciliation conclusion.
Test that every break the preparer explained has evidence behind the explanation, not just a narrative.
List any valuation date where the run proceeded on an unexplained break as an automatic exception.
testing.done: in-force reconciliations are independently recomputed against tolerance and every break explanation is evidenced or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100 percent of segments valued on principle-based reserves and 100 percent of segments with a methodology or assumption change in the year.
Take a seeded random sample of 30 individual policies stratified across plan code, issue year and duration from the year-end in-force.
Take 100 percent of post-close reserve adjustments.
Record the seed, population sizes, sample sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers all principle-based and changed segments, all post-close adjustments and a reproducible stratified policy sample.

testing.step: Reproduce the year-end reserve from the recorded versions
actions: Restore the recorded data version, assumption set version and model version for two sampled segments and re-run the valuation yourself.
Compare your reserve to the certified figure and require agreement to the stated reproduction tolerance rather than to the nearest round number.
Where reproduction fails, determine whether the cause is an unrecorded version, a manual output adjustment or an untracked model change, and name it.
Capture the run ids of your reproduction runs into the workpaper.
testing.done: two segments are re-run from recorded versions and either reproduce the certified reserve within tolerance or the reproduction failure cause is named.

testing.step: Recalculate sampled policy reserves independently
actions: For each of the 30 sampled policies rebuild the reserve outside the model using the prescribed table, interest rate and method for its issue year, or the projected cash flows for principle-based segments.
Compare your figure to the model output per policy and investigate every difference above the per-policy tolerance.
Check the plan code to valuation basis mapping is right for the issue year, since a stale mapping is the usual cause of a systematically wrong reserve.
Extend any error pattern found across the full population of that plan code and quantify the total effect.
testing.done: each sampled policy has an independently rebuilt reserve, and any error found is extended across its plan code with the total effect quantified.

testing.step: Test assumption governance and prescribed element currency
actions: Compare the assumption set used in each sampled run to the approved set and list every parameter that differs.
Confirm each change carries a written approval dated before assumption lock and an experience study behind it.

Verify the prescribed elements against their published sources — the valuation mortality table and margins for the issue year, the published risk-free curve for the valuation date, the prescribed scenario set version — and flag any stale version.
Treat any assumption applied without prior approval as a fail regardless of whether it increased or decreased the reserve.
testing.done: every assumption used matches an approved, experience-supported version and every prescribed element matches its published source for the valuation date.

testing.step: Recompute the movement analysis and the basis bridges
actions: Recompute the reserve walk components from the underlying runs and compare each component to the reported walk.
Re-derive the model change component by running current data and assumptions through the prior model version and compare to the reported isolation.
Recompute the statutory to IFRS 17 and statutory to Solvency II bridges and confirm every reconciling item is quantified and explained.
List any component whose reported figure cannot be derived from the runs as an exception.
testing.done: each movement component and each basis bridge is independently recomputed from the runs, with unsupported components listed.

testing.step: Trace certified reserves to the ledger and the filed statement
actions: Take the Appointed Actuary certified schedule and trace each segment total to the posted reserve journal by run id reference.
Trace the ledger total to Exhibit 5 and Exhibit 6 in the filed annual statement and to the technical provisions in the solvency return.
Confirm the journal approver differed from the preparer and that no reserve journal was posted after the certified schedule date without a Chief Actuary approval.
Quantify any difference between certified, posted and filed reserves and state whether it affects surplus or risk-based capital.
testing.done: certified, posted and filed reserves agree by run id reference, with any difference quantified against surplus and capital.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the valuation date, segment, basis and the reserve amount affected.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — data break unexplained, assumption unapproved, model version unvalidated, run not reproducible, mapping stale, output manually adjusted, post-close adjustment unapproved — and name a single owner.
Set a remediation date and mark whether the exception requires a prior-period restatement or a current-period correction.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a quantified reserve effect, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner and a restatement decision.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the valuation test
actions: State the results: segments reproduced, policies recalculated within tolerance, assumption changes approved on time and reconciliations inside the 0.1 percent tolerance.
Write the conclusion — reserves computed in accordance with the prescribed valuation standards, in accordance with exceptions, or not in accordance — with workpaper references behind each fail.
Have the independent reviewer, who built, calibrated and ran none of the tested models, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the board risk committee and to the Appointed Actuary before the actuarial opinion is signed, and file the workpaper in the model governance repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the reproduction and recalculation results with a conclusion, delivered to the committee and the Appointed Actuary before the opinion is signed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Appointed Actuary personally signs the opinion and owns the supporting memorandum; the board makes the appointment and the Chief Actuary provides the resourcing behind it

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 8 Standards 8.3 and 8.8 on the actuarial function and its reporting to the board, read against the current ICP text and cross-walked to the wording rules actually applied: NAIC Valuation Manual VM-30 Statement of Actuarial Opinion, the Actuarial Opinion and Memorandum Regulation, the qualified actuary definition in VM-01, and Actuarial Standards of Practice 22, 36 and 41

In-scope processes.value: Annual actuarial opinion cycle for every insurance entity requiring one: appointment and qualification confirmation, scope and reliance determination, opinion wording, the supporting actuarial memorandum, the regulatory asset adequacy issues summary and board reporting

In-scope systems.value: Valuation and asset adequacy runs behind the opinion; the signed opinion, memorandum and reliance letters are held in the compliance evidence repository and tabled through the board portal

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statement of Actuarial Opinion Procedure — appointment and qualification, scope determination, reliance letters, opinion wording by type, memorandum content standard, asset adequacy summary and the board reporting and filing steps

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the board on the recommendation of the Chief Actuary; the appointment of the Appointed Actuary is a board resolution and cannot be delegated to management

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Statement of Actuarial Opinion signed and filed with the annual statement by 1 March; the supporting actuarial memorandum prepared by 1 March and available to the commissioner on request by 1 July; the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary due by 15 March; the VM-31 report due by 1 April; a change of Appointed Actuary notified to the commissioner within 5 business days with the reasons letter to follow

Deadline reminders configured.value: Actuarial calendar alerts the Appointed Actuary at 45, 20 and 5 days before 1 March, opens the memorandum drafting task on 15 January, and opens the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary task the day the opinion is signed so 15 March is not missed

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed opinion, actuarial memorandum, asset adequacy summary, reliance letters, qualification documentation and the board appointment resolution retained 7 years from the opinion date in the compliance evidence repository, indexed by entity, opinion year and actuary

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A qualified, adverse or inconclusive opinion, an opinion signed without a current appointment, a missing reliance letter or a late memorandum is logged with the cause, the regulator informed and the corrective action

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Actuary signs off any correction or reissue of an opinion or memorandum, and the board is informed of any opinion that is not unqualified

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every entity requiring a Statement of Actuarial Opinion for the year, with its opinion, memorandum, asset adequacy summary, reliance letters and the reserve figures the opinion covers

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on form and support — an opinion signed by an actuary without a current board appointment or without meeting the qualified actuary standard is a fail; a missing scope, reliance or opinion paragraph is a fail; a reserve figure in the opinion that does not agree to the filed statement is a fail; a memorandum not prepared by 1 March is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual per entity; the test runs annually in the window between the opinion signing and the 1 July memorandum availability date, so any defect can still be corrected with the regulator

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not be the Appointed Actuary or a member of the team that produced the opinion or the memorandum

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual actuarial opinion test workpaper — qualification check, wording comparison, reserve tie-out, reliance letter trace and exception log — in the compliance evidence repository under the opinion year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Signed opinion as filed, the actuarial memorandum, the asset adequacy issues summary, reliance letters and the qualification documentation, producible for the domiciliary commissioner within 5 business days of a request and in any case by 1 July

Regulator response path.value: Appointed Actuary responds personally to opinion and memorandum questions with the Chief Actuary informed; the CFO and General Counsel are engaged before any response touching a qualified opinion or a reserve restatement, and the board risk committee chair is told the same day

checklist.step: Confirm the appointment and the qualification of the signing actuary
actions: Locate the board resolution appointing the Appointed Actuary for the entity and confirm it is current and names the individual, not a firm.

Confirm the actuary meets the qualified actuary standard — membership of the recognised professional body, the specific qualification standard for the opinion type, and the continuing education hours logged for the year.
Check no disciplinary action or practice restriction applies and record the check date.
Where the appointment changed in the year, confirm the commissioner was notified within 5 business days and that the reasons letter and the former actuary response were filed.
File the resolution, the qualification evidence and the continuing education log to the opinion year folder.
checklist.done: a current board resolution, qualification evidence and a continuing education log are on file for the signing actuary, with any change properly notified.

checklist.step: Fix the scope of the opinion before the work starts
actions: List every reserve and liability item the opinion must cover — aggregate reserves for life policies and contracts, deposit-type contract funds, policy and contract claims, premium and other deposit funds — by annual statement exhibit and line.
Identify items excluded from the opinion and state the reason and who opines on them instead.
Confirm which entities in the group need their own opinion and which are covered by a parent opinion, checking each state requirement rather than assuming.
Agree the scope in writing with the Chief Actuary and the Controller so the statement lines and the opinion lines cannot diverge.
checklist.done: the opinion scope names every covered exhibit line, states every exclusion with a reason, and is agreed in writing before work begins.

checklist.step: Obtain the reliance letters for data and for other work
actions: Request a signed data reliance letter from the officer responsible for the in-force and claims data, stating the data was prepared for this purpose and is accurate and complete.
Request reliance letters for investment data from the Chief Investment Officer and for reinsurance data from the Reinsurance Manager where the opinion depends on them.
Where another actuary produced part of the work, obtain their reliance statement naming the segments and the standards they applied.
Perform your own data review sufficient to accept the reliance, testing reasonableness and consistency rather than accepting the letter alone, and document what you did.
checklist.done: signed reliance letters cover data, investments, reinsurance and any other actuary work, and the actuary own review supporting each reliance is documented.

checklist.step: Confirm the reserves the opinion will cover are final
actions: Obtain the final certified valuation schedule with the run ids and check it matches the version the Controller posted to the ledger.
Tie every reserve figure that will appear in the opinion to the corresponding annual statement exhibit and line, cell by cell.
Confirm no post-close adjustment has moved a covered figure since the schedule was certified, and re-tie if one has.
Freeze the figures for the opinion and note the date and time of the freeze.
checklist.done: every figure that will appear in the opinion ties to the filed statement exhibit line and to a frozen certified valuation schedule.

checklist.step: Test the reserves against the minimum standards and the asset adequacy conclusion
actions: Confirm reserves meet or exceed the minimum required by the applicable valuation law, table and interest basis for each issue year, and record any deficiency and the additional reserve held.
Take the asset adequacy analysis conclusion from the cash-flow testing work and confirm it supports an opinion that reserves make good and sufficient provision under moderately adverse conditions.
Where any scenario or segment shows a deficiency, quantify the additional reserve established and confirm it is in the filed figures.
Document the basis for the going-forward conclusion including any material subsequent event you considered.
checklist.done: reserves are confirmed at or above the statutory minimum, the asset adequacy conclusion is documented, and any deficiency has a quantified additional reserve in the filed figures.

checklist.step: Draft the opinion in the prescribed sections and wording
actions: Draft the Identification section naming the actuary, the appointment, the relationship to the company and the qualification claim.
Draft the Scope section listing the exhibit lines covered with the amounts, and the Reliance section naming each person relied upon and the letter date.

Draft the Opinion section with the prescribed assertions — reserves computed in accordance with accepted actuarial standards and the applicable law, based on assumptions producing reserves at least as great as those required, meeting the requirements of the state of domicile, and making good and sufficient provision.
Select the opinion type deliberately — unqualified, qualified, adverse or inconclusive — and where it is not unqualified state the reason in the wording rather than in a covering note.
Include the asset adequacy paragraph and the required standard actuarial opinion wording for the applicable jurisdiction.
checklist.done: the drafted opinion contains the Identification, Scope, Reliance and Opinion sections with the prescribed assertions and a deliberately chosen opinion type.

checklist.step: Write the supporting actuarial memorandum
actions: Write the memorandum to be prepared by 1 March covering the reserve methodology by segment, the asset adequacy method, the assets used and how they were assigned, the assumptions with their support and the sensitivity results.
Document the reinvestment and disinvestment assumptions and the assumed spreads and default costs on projected reinvested assets, since this is what regulators press on for complex assets.
Show the results by scenario and by segment, name the deficient scenarios and state the additional reserves held.
Include the reconciliation from the prior year opinion, listing every method and assumption change with its effect.
Have a second actuary review the memorandum against the content standard before it is finalised.
checklist.done: a memorandum prepared by 1 March covers method, assets, assumptions, reinvestment assumptions, scenario results and prior year changes, and is peer reviewed.

checklist.step: Prepare the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary
actions: Summarise the material issues from the asset adequacy analysis, the scenarios that failed and the reserve strengthening or other action taken, for filing by 15 March.
Compare the current results to the prior year and explain any material change in the margin between assets and reserve requirement.
State the sensitivity of the conclusion to the assumptions most likely to be challenged, such as reinvestment rates, lapse and mortality improvement.
Have the Chief Actuary read the summary against the memorandum so the two cannot tell different stories.
checklist.done: the summary states the failed scenarios, actions taken, prior year comparison and key sensitivities, and is consistent with the memorandum, by 15 March.

checklist.step: Run the independent peer review of the opinion package
actions: Read the drafted opinion against the prescribed wording line by line and flag every omitted or altered assertion.
Tie every amount in the Scope section to the annual statement exhibit line independently.
Confirm each person named in the Reliance section has a signed letter on file dated before the opinion date.
Challenge the opinion type against the evidence, specifically whether any scope limitation or unresolved deficiency should have produced a qualification.
Record the review findings and their disposition with your name and date.
checklist.done: the peer review records a wording comparison, an independent amount tie-out, a reliance letter check and a challenge of the opinion type, with findings dispositioned.

checklist.step: Report the opinion and the actuarial function findings to the board
actions: Table the draft opinion, the memorandum summary and the asset adequacy issues to the board or its risk committee before the opinion is signed.
State the actuarial function opinion on technical provisions, pricing adequacy, capital adequacy and reinsurance, which ICP 8 expects to reach the board.
Escalate explicitly any matter that would make the opinion other than unqualified and record the board response.
Minute the board receipt and any decision taken, and record the minute reference on the opinion file.
checklist.done: the board has received the draft opinion and the actuarial function findings before signing, with the minute reference recorded.

checklist.step: Sign the opinion and lock the package
actions: Sign and date the opinion no earlier than the date the covered figures were frozen and no later than the annual statement filing date of 1 March.
Confirm the signed version is the peer reviewed version by comparing the document hash or version id, not by reading the first page.
Lock the memorandum and the supporting workpapers against edit on the signing date, allowing changes only as a dated addendum.
Hand the signed opinion to Regulatory Reporting for insertion into the annual statement and confirm receipt.
checklist.done: the opinion is signed and dated inside the window on the peer reviewed version, the package is locked, and Regulatory Reporting has confirmed receipt.

checklist.step: Hold the memorandum ready for the commissioner request
actions: File the memorandum, the asset adequacy summary and the supporting exhibits in the repository the day the opinion is signed.
Confirm the package can be produced to the commissioner on request and in any case by 1 July, and record who can produce it if the actuary is unavailable.
Prepare a short index to the memorandum so an examiner can find the method, assumption, asset and scenario sections without asking.
Log any commissioner request with the date received, what was sent and the date sent.
checklist.done: the memorandum package is filed, indexed, producible by 1 July, and every commissioner request is logged with what was sent and when.

checklist.step: Handle a qualified, adverse or inconclusive opinion
actions: Where the opinion cannot be unqualified, document the specific reserves or scope affected and the quantified effect where it can be quantified.
Inform the CFO, the General Counsel and the board risk committee chair on the day the conclusion is reached, before the opinion is filed.
Agree the regulator communication plan with the domiciliary department, including whether a meeting should precede the filing.
Open a remediation plan naming what must change for the next opinion to be unqualified, with owners and dates.
checklist.done: any non-unqualified opinion has a quantified explanation, same-day executive and board notification, an agreed regulator communication plan and a dated remediation plan.

checklist.step: Manage a change of Appointed Actuary on the regulatory clock
actions: On any resignation or replacement, pass the board resolution appointing the successor and notify the commissioner within 5 business days that the appointment has ended.
File the letter stating whether there were any disagreements with the former actuary in the preceding twenty four months on reserve methodology, assumptions or scope, and how they were resolved.
Send the letter to the former actuary and file their written response with the commissioner.
Arrange a documented handover of workpapers, models and assumption rationale to the successor before the next valuation date.
checklist.done: the change is notified within 5 business days, the disagreements letter and the former actuary response are filed, and a documented handover is complete.

checklist.step: Retain the opinion year package
actions: File the signed opinion as filed, the memorandum, the asset adequacy issues summary, the reliance letters, the qualification evidence, the board resolution and the peer review notes.
Apply the 7-years-from-opinion-date retention label and mark the package legal-hold-eligible.
Confirm the package is retrievable by legal entity, opinion year, Appointed Actuary name and opinion type.
Record the opinion type against the entity in the register so a run of qualified opinions is visible over time.
checklist.done: the opinion year package is retained for 7 years, retrievable by entity, year, actuary and opinion type, with the type recorded in the register.

testing.step: Build the population of entities requiring an opinion and the packages produced
actions: Rebuild from the licence register the list of entities that owe a Statement of Actuarial Opinion for the year, rather than taking the actuarial calendar as given.
Match each to the opinion, memorandum, asset adequacy summary and reliance letters actually produced.
List every entity with no opinion, no memorandum or an incomplete package as an automatic exception.
Sign the population as complete with the register extract date and the record count.
testing.done: the population is rebuilt from the licence register, matched to produced packages, and every gap is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Reconcile opinion amounts to the filed annual statement
actions: Take every amount in the Scope section of each opinion and trace it to the corresponding exhibit and line in the filed annual statement.
Confirm the total opined reserves agree to the aggregate reserves in the filed statement with no unexplained difference.
Trace the same amounts back to the certified valuation schedule and the run id behind it.
Treat any difference between opined, filed and certified figures as a fail rather than a presentation issue.
testing.done: every Scope amount ties to the filed statement line and to the certified valuation run id, or is recorded as a fail.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100 percent of opinions that are not unqualified and 100 percent of entities whose Appointed Actuary changed in the year.
Take 100 percent of segments where the memorandum reports a failed scenario or an additional reserve.
Take a seeded random sample of 10 reliance letters and 10 memorandum assumption sections across the remaining entities.
Record the seed, population sizes, sample sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers all non-unqualified opinions, actuary changes and failed scenarios plus a reproducible random selection.

testing.step: Re-perform the qualification and appointment check
actions: Open the board resolution for each sampled entity and confirm it names the signing individual and was in force on the opinion date.
Verify professional body membership and the qualification standard claimed directly with the published register rather than with the actuary own statement.
Recount the continuing education hours against the requirement for the year and check the relevant-topic split.
For any change of actuary recompute the 5 business day notification clock and confirm the disagreements letter and the former actuary response are on file.
testing.done: each signing actuary is independently confirmed as appointed and qualified on the opinion date, with change notifications recomputed.

testing.step: Compare the opinion wording to the prescribed text
actions: Set the filed opinion side by side with the prescribed wording for the jurisdiction and mark every assertion present, altered or missing.
Confirm the Identification, Scope, Reliance and Opinion sections all exist and that the Reliance section names every person relied upon.
Check the opinion type stated matches the substance — a scope limitation described in the body with an unqualified conclusion is a fail.
Confirm the signature date sits on or after the figure freeze and on or before 1 March.
testing.done: the wording comparison records every altered or missing assertion, the opinion type matches the substance, and the signature date is inside the window.

testing.step: Trace every reliance to a signed letter and to the actuary own review
actions: For each sampled reliance, open the signed letter and confirm the signatory holds the responsibility claimed and the letter is dated before the opinion.
Confirm the letter states the data was prepared for this purpose and asserts accuracy and completeness rather than merely transmitting a file.
Find the documented review the actuary performed to accept the reliance and confirm it tested reasonableness, not just receipt.
List any reliance with no letter, a post-dated letter or no supporting review as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled reliance has a pre-dated signed letter with the required assertions and a documented acceptance review, or is listed.

testing.step: Test the memorandum content against the standard
actions: Check the memorandum was prepared by 1 March using the document version history, not the cover date typed on it.

Confirm it covers each required area — method by segment, asset assignment, assumptions with support, reinvestment and disinvestment assumptions with spreads and default costs, scenario results, sensitivities and the prior year reconciliation.
Re-derive two sensitivity results from the underlying runs and compare to the reported figures.
List any required area covered by a single sentence with no support as a content exception.
testing.done: the memorandum preparation date is evidenced from version history, every required area is present with support, and two sensitivities are independently re-derived.

testing.step: Recompute the filing clocks and confirm the lodgements
actions: Recompute the 1 March opinion filing date, the 15 March asset adequacy issues summary date and the 1 April principle-based reserving report date from each entity financial year end.
Confirm the opinion physically appears in the filed annual statement in the required position and that the filed copy is the signed version.
Confirm the asset adequacy issues summary was lodged by 15 March and capture the receipt.
Confirm the memorandum could be produced by 1 July by requesting it from the repository yourself and timing the retrieval.
testing.done: all filing clocks are recomputed per entity, the signed opinion is present in the filed statement, and memorandum retrieval is tested and timed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the entity, the opinion year, the section or document affected and the amount where one is involved.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — appointment lapsed, qualification unevidenced, wording altered, reliance letter missing, memorandum late or thin, amount mismatch, summary not lodged — and name a single owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any amount mismatch with the filed statement, open an amended filing assessment with the Controller the same day.
Carry every open exception into next year test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a date and, for amount mismatches, an opened amended filing assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the opinion test
actions: State the counts: opinions due, signed by a qualified appointed actuary, filed on time, memoranda prepared by 1 March and summaries lodged by 15 March.
Write the conclusion — the actuarial opinion obligation is met, met with exceptions, or not met — with the workpaper references behind each fail.
Have the independent reviewer, who is not the Appointed Actuary and produced none of the tested documents, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee and the board risk committee before the 1 July memorandum availability date and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the counts and conclusion, is reported to both committees before 1 July, and is filed in the repository.
