Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 8 Standards 8.3 and 8.8 on reporting from the control functions to the supervisor and the board, read against the current ICP text and cross-walked to the lodgement rules applied: the NAIC Annual Statement Instructions for the current statement year, VM-30 requiring the Statement of Actuarial Opinion to accompany the annual statement, and the Solvency II quantitative reporting template submission rules

In-scope processes.value: Annual statement lodgement for every licensed entity: statement assembly, opinion insertion, officer signature and notarisation, electronic submission to the NAIC and to each state of domicile and licensure, fee payment, supplemental filings and the capture of every confirmation

In-scope systems.value: Statement preparation and electronic lodgement to the NAIC Financial Data Repository and the state departments; confirmations and receipts are filed to the financial reporting repository and tracked on the filing calendar

Compliance procedure documented.value: Annual Statement and Opinion Lodgement Procedure — per-state filing checklist review, statement assembly and bar coding, opinion insertion and signature control, submission sequence, fee payment channel, receipt capture and the amended filing route

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and refreshed each December against the new statement year instructions and each state current filing checklist before the cycle starts

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual statement with the Statement of Actuarial Opinion due 1 March to the NAIC and every state of licensure; risk-based capital report due 1 March; the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary 15 March; Management Discussion and Analysis and other 1 April supplements; the audited report 1 June; quarterly statements 15 May, 15 August and 15 November; Solvency II annual templates at 14 weeks after year end

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar alerts the Regulatory Reporting Manager at 30, 14, 7 and 2 days before 1 March per entity, opens the opinion insertion task the day the Appointed Actuary signs, and pages the CFO on 1 March plus 1 business day for any jurisdiction without a confirmation

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Filed statement PDFs as lodged, the inserted signed opinion, jurat signature pages, submission confirmations, fee receipts and state acknowledgements retained 7 years from filing in the financial reporting repository, indexed by entity, statement year and jurisdiction

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A jurisdiction not filed, a filing lodged without the opinion attached, a rejected or unvalidated submission, an unpaid fee or a late supplement is logged with days late, the jurisdiction, the corrective filing date and the root cause

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs off every late filing, every amended statement and any decision to file on an approved extension

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every licensed entity and every jurisdiction it is licensed in, crossed with every annual and supplemental filing due for the statement year, including the opinion, the risk-based capital report and the asset adequacy issues summary

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any jurisdiction of licensure not filed, any statement lodged without the signed opinion attached in the required position, any submission without a captured confirmation, or any filing after its statutory date without approved relief is a fail escalated to the CFO the same day

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual with quarterly interim statements; the test runs once after 1 April when the annual and the 1 March and 15 March deliverables have all matured, with a light quarterly check on the 15 May, 15 August and 15 November lodgements

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have assembled or lodged any tested filing and must sit outside the Regulatory Reporting team

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual lodgement completeness workpaper — licence register to filing matrix, confirmation trace, opinion attachment check and exception log — in the compliance evidence repository under the statement year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Statement as filed with the opinion in place, the jurat signature page, the submission confirmation and the fee receipt, producible per jurisdiction within 5 business days of a department request or an examination call letter

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager answers lodgement and completeness questions; the Appointed Actuary answers any question on the opinion content and the CFO clears any late-filing or amended-filing explanation before it is sent

checklist.step: Refresh the licence register and the jurisdiction filing matrix
actions: Pull the current certificates of authority per entity and list every state or country where the entity is licensed, including states where writing has ceased but the licence is retained.
Build the matrix of entity by jurisdiction by filing type — annual statement, actuarial opinion, risk-based capital report, asset adequacy issues summary, supplements — for the statement year.
Confirm each line against the state current annual statement filing checklist, which changes yearly, and note where a hard copy or an original signature is still required.
Record whether the jurisdiction accepts the NAIC electronic filing alone or requires a separate department submission, and name the account holder for each portal.
Publish the matrix to Finance and Actuarial with the owner and the due date on every line.
checklist.done: the matrix covers every licensed jurisdiction and filing type for the year, checked against each state current filing checklist, with owners named.

checklist.step: Refresh the procedure against the new statement year instructions
actions: Read the current NAIC Annual Statement Instructions for the line of business and list every change from the prior year — new exhibits, changed interrogatories, revised bar code requirements and new supplements.
Update the internal preparation procedure and the exhibit ownership list for each change and circulate the diff to the preparers.
Confirm the statement preparation software has been updated to the current statement year version and that its validation rule set is current.
Brief Actuarial and Investments on any change that affects the exhibits they source.
checklist.done: the procedure and software are on the current statement year with every instruction change listed and circulated to the affected preparers.

checklist.step: Assemble the statement and clear every validation
actions: Load the final trial balance, actuarial exhibits, investment schedules and reinsurance schedules into the statement software and complete every page and interrogatory.
Run the full validation and cross-check set and clear every error; document the reason for any warning left open on the exception page.
Confirm the bar code pages are produced for each filing type the jurisdiction requires so a submission is not rejected on assembly grounds.
Circulate the near-final statement to the Appointed Actuary, the Chief Investment Officer and the Reinsurance Manager for exhibit confirmation.
Freeze the version to be filed and record its version id.
checklist.done: every page and interrogatory is complete, all validations are cleared or documented, bar codes are produced and the filing version is frozen.

checklist.step: Insert the signed actuarial opinion in the required position
actions: Take the signed opinion PDF from the Appointed Actuary and confirm the signature, the date and the entity name before touching the statement.
Insert the opinion at the position the statement instructions require, immediately following the jurat page, and confirm the pagination and bar coding still validate.
Tie every amount in the opinion Scope section to the corresponding exhibit line in the assembled statement and stop if any figure differs.
Confirm the opinion inserted is the signed version and not a draft, by comparing the version id or document hash.
Record the insertion and the check on the filing calendar line.
checklist.done: the signed opinion sits in the required position, its Scope amounts tie to the statement exhibits, and the inserted version is confirmed as the signed one.

checklist.step: Obtain the officer signatures and any required notarisation
actions: Route the jurat page for the signatures the instructions require — typically the president or chief executive, the secretary and the treasurer or chief financial officer.
Confirm each signatory holds the office named on the date of signature against the corporate register, since an officer change mid-cycle invalidates a pre-signed page.
Arrange notarisation or a wet signature where the jurisdiction still requires it and allow the courier time inside the 1 March window.
File the executed jurat page to the filing folder and confirm the electronic version matches it.
checklist.done: the jurat carries the required officer signatures verified against the corporate register, with notarisation obtained where required, before submission.

checklist.step: Lodge to the NAIC and to the domiciliary department
actions: Submit the annual statement electronically to the NAIC Financial Data Repository for the statement year and capture the submission confirmation number and timestamp.
Submit to the domiciliary department through its required channel, whether the NAIC filing suffices or a separate department portal upload is needed.
Confirm the submission passed the receiving validation and was not merely uploaded, since an upload that fails validation is not a filing.
Attach the confirmation to the filing calendar line the same day and treat any line without a confirmation as unfiled.
Complete every submission on or before 1 March rather than lodging on the day, so a rejection can still be corrected.
checklist.done: the NAIC and domiciliary submissions are validated and confirmed, with confirmation numbers attached to the calendar lines on or before 1 March.

checklist.step: Work the foreign state filings jurisdiction by jurisdiction
actions: For each non-domiciliary state of licensure, follow its checklist: electronic only, electronic plus a signed hard copy, or a department portal upload with a state transmittal form.
Pay the filing fee through the channel the state requires, capturing the payment confirmation and matching it to the invoice or fee schedule amount.
Complete any state-specific supplement the checklist names, such as a state page, a premium tax related exhibit or a certificate of compliance.
Chase any state that has not acknowledged within 5 business days and record who you contacted and when.
checklist.done: every non-domiciliary state line shows the checklist followed, the fee paid with a receipt and an acknowledgement or a recorded chase.

checklist.step: Lodge the risk-based capital report on the same clock
actions: Prepare the risk-based capital report from the filed statement figures so the two cannot disagree, and reconcile the total adjusted capital and the authorised control level to the statement.
Confirm the risk-based capital result and identify whether any action level is triggered, since that changes what must be filed and to whom.
Submit the report by 1 March to the NAIC and the domiciliary commissioner and capture the confirmation.
Where a company action level or worse is indicated, notify the CFO and General Counsel the same day and start the required plan on its own clock.
checklist.done: the risk-based capital report reconciles to the filed statement, is lodged by 1 March with a confirmation, and any action level trigger is escalated the same day.

checklist.step: Lodge the asset adequacy issues summary and the other dated supplements
actions: Lodge the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary supplied by the Appointed Actuary by 15 March and capture the confirmation.
Work the 1 April supplements from the instructions list, including the management discussion and analysis and any certification of reasonableness the state requires.
Lodge the principle-based reserving actuarial report by 1 April where the entity has principle-based segments.
Reconcile the supplement list filed to the instructions list and close each calendar line only against a confirmation.
checklist.done: the 15 March summary and every 1 April supplement are lodged with confirmations, reconciled to the instructions list.

checklist.step: Lodge the international and group returns carrying the opinion equivalents
actions: Submit the annual Solvency II quantitative reporting templates at 14 weeks after year end through the supervisor portal, passing the published validation rule set before submission.
Submit the actuarial function report and the equivalent appointed actuary report in each jurisdiction that requires one, on its own statutory date.
Reconcile technical provisions across the statutory, solvency and group returns and document each reconciling item so a supervisor sees one story.
Capture every acknowledgement and file it against the entity and return type.
checklist.done: each international and group return is lodged on its own date with validations passed, acknowledgements captured and technical provisions reconciled across bases.

checklist.step: Reconcile the filing matrix to confirmations after each deadline
actions: At 1 March plus 1 business day, run the matrix against captured confirmations and list every line without one.
Repeat at 15 March, 1 April and after each quarterly date so a gap is found in days, not at the next examination.
Open an exception for each gap with the jurisdiction, the filing type, the days late and the assigned owner.
Report the completeness position to the CFO after each deadline, including a clean report.
checklist.done: the matrix is reconciled to confirmations within one business day of each deadline and every gap is an open, owned exception.

checklist.step: Handle rejections, resubmissions and amended filings
actions: On any rejection, read the validation or department message, fix the underlying data or assembly defect rather than re-uploading the same file, and resubmit.
Where a filed figure must change, prepare an amended statement marked as an amendment with a cover letter explaining what changed and why, and obtain CFO sign-off before lodging.
Notify the Appointed Actuary where an amendment touches a figure covered by the opinion, so the opinion can be reissued if it must be.
Record the original filing date, the rejection date and the accepted resubmission date on the calendar line so the true timeliness is visible.
checklist.done: each rejection is fixed at source and resubmitted, each amendment carries a CFO-approved cover letter, and the calendar shows original and accepted dates.

checklist.step: Answer department queries on the filing inside their window
actions: Log every department query with the jurisdiction, the date received, the response due date and the internal owner.
Route questions on reserves and the opinion to the Appointed Actuary and questions on investments to the Chief Investment Officer, keeping the response single-voiced through Regulatory Reporting.
Have the CFO clear any response that changes a filed figure or concedes an error before it is sent.
File the query, the response and the department closure on the entity and year record.
checklist.done: every query has a logged due date, a routed owner, a cleared response where a figure moved, and a filed closure.

checklist.step: Track licence changes that add or remove a filing obligation
actions: Monitor new licences, licence surrenders, redomestications and mergers during the year and update the filing matrix within 5 business days of each.
Confirm a surrendered licence still requires a final statement filing where the state demands one, rather than dropping the line immediately.
Confirm a newly licensed state is added with its full filing checklist before its first 1 March.
Reconcile the matrix to the licence register quarterly so the annual cycle never opens on a stale list.
checklist.done: every licence change updates the matrix within 5 business days and a quarterly reconciliation to the licence register is evidenced.

checklist.step: Retain the lodged set and close the statement year
actions: File per entity, year and jurisdiction the statement as filed, the inserted signed opinion, the jurat page, the confirmation, the fee receipt and any acknowledgement or query closure.
Apply the 7-years-from-filing retention label and mark the set legal-hold-eligible.
Confirm the set is retrievable by entity, statement year, jurisdiction and filing type, and that the as-filed copy is the version that was actually accepted.
Close every calendar line to a final status of filed, filed late, amended or relieved, so next year opens from a known state.
checklist.done: the lodged set is retained for 7 years, retrievable by entity, year and jurisdiction, with every calendar line closed to a final status.

testing.step: Build the population of jurisdictions and filings owed for the statement year
actions: Rebuild the entity by jurisdiction list from the certificates of authority rather than from the filing matrix, so a jurisdiction dropped from the matrix is visible.
Derive from the current statement year instructions and each state checklist the filings owed per line — statement, opinion, risk-based capital report, asset adequacy summary, supplements.
Add every filing lodged in the year from the submission logs, including amendments and resubmissions.
Reconcile owed to lodged and sign the population as complete with the extract date and record counts.
testing.done: the owed-filings population is rebuilt from certificates of authority and state checklists and reconciled to the lodgement log.

testing.step: Reconcile every owed filing to a captured confirmation
actions: Open the confirmation for each owed filing rather than reading the calendar status, and check it names the right entity, statement year and filing type.
Compare the confirmation timestamp to the statutory date and compute days early or late for every line.
List every line with no confirmation, a confirmation for a rejected submission, or a confirmation dated after the deadline without relief as an automatic exception.
Check that any resubmission after a rejection has its own accepted confirmation, since a rejected submission is not a filing.
testing.done: every owed filing traces to an opened, correctly scoped confirmation with a computed days-late figure, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100 percent of domiciliary filings, all amended filings and every filing that was rejected at least once.
Take a seeded random sample of 15 non-domiciliary jurisdiction lines spread across at least three submission channels.
Take 100 percent of risk-based capital reports and asset adequacy issues summaries.
Record the seed, population size, sample size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers all domiciliary, amended and rejected filings plus a reproducible spread of non-domiciliary jurisdictions.

testing.step: Re-perform the opinion attachment and position check on the filed document
actions: Retrieve the document as accepted by the regulator, not the internal copy, for each sampled filing.
Confirm the Statement of Actuarial Opinion is present, signed, dated and positioned where the current statement year instructions require.
Confirm the signature is the Appointed Actuary named in the board resolution and that the opinion names the correct entity and year.
Record any filing where the opinion is absent, unsigned, a draft version or out of position as a fail.
testing.done: each sampled accepted filing is confirmed to carry the signed opinion in the required position, or the defect is recorded as a fail.

testing.step: Tie the opinion and statement figures to the certified valuation
actions: Trace each amount in the opinion Scope section to the exhibit line in the accepted statement and to the ledger reserve balance.
Trace the ledger balance back to the Appointed Actuary certified schedule and its run id.
Recompute total adjusted capital and the authorised control level in the risk-based capital report from the accepted statement figures and compare to the report as filed.
Quantify any difference and state whether it changes the risk-based capital action level.
testing.done: opinion, statement, ledger and certified valuation figures agree by run id, and the recomputed risk-based capital result matches the filed report.

testing.step: Verify the jurat signatures and officer authority
actions: Open the jurat page of each sampled accepted filing and list the signatories and their stated offices.
Confirm each signatory held that office on the signature date against the corporate register and the board minutes.
Confirm notarisation is present where the jurisdiction requires it and that the notary date is not before the officer signature date.
Flag any pre-signed page reused after an officer change as a fail.
testing.done: every sampled jurat is confirmed signed by officers holding the stated office on that date, with notarisation where required.

testing.step: Recompute every statutory lodgement clock
actions: Recompute the 1 March statement and opinion date, the 1 March risk-based capital date, the 15 March asset adequacy summary date and the 1 April supplement dates from each entity year end.
Recompute the Solvency II 14 week annual template date and compare to the portal submission timestamp.
Recompute the quarterly 15 May, 15 August and 15 November dates and check each quarterly lodgement against them.
List every clock missed with the days late, the jurisdiction and whether the miss was self-identified or raised by the department.
testing.done: all annual, supplemental, quarterly and solvency clocks are recomputed per entity and every miss is quantified in days.

testing.step: Test fees, rejections and query handling
actions: For each sampled jurisdiction match the fee paid to the published fee schedule amount and to a payment receipt, listing under and over payments.
Trace each rejection to the defect that caused it, the fix applied and the accepted resubmission, and flag any case where the same file was simply re-uploaded.
Trace every department query to a dated response inside the stated window and to a recorded closure.
Confirm each amended filing carries a CFO-approved cover letter and that the Appointed Actuary was informed where an opined figure changed.
testing.done: fees match the published schedules with receipts, every rejection traces to a real fix, and queries and amendments are properly documented.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the entity, jurisdiction, filing type and the days late or the defect found.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — jurisdiction missing from the matrix, checklist not refreshed, confirmation never captured, opinion not inserted, jurat authority stale, validation rejection unresolved, fee unpaid — and name a single owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any unfiled jurisdiction, lodge the late filing and notify the department the same week with a CFO-approved explanation.
Carry every open exception into next year test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a date, and any unfiled jurisdiction is lodged and explained the same week.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the lodgement test
actions: State the counts: jurisdiction filings owed, confirmed on time, confirmed late with days, amended and unfiled.
Write the conclusion — the annual statement and opinion lodgement obligation is met, met with exceptions, or not met — with workpaper references behind each fail.
Have the independent reviewer, who assembled and lodged none of the tested filings, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the owed, on-time, late, amended and unfiled counts with a conclusion, reported to the committee and filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Appointed Actuary owns the asset adequacy conclusion supporting the opinion; the ALM / Asset-Liability Actuary owns the asset modelling and the cash-flow testing runs behind it

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 8 Standard 8.7 on the actuarial function evaluating technical provisions, premium and pricing adequacy, capital adequacy and reinsurance and reporting material findings to the board, read against the current ICP text and cross-walked to the asset adequacy rules applied: VM-30 Section 3, the Actuarial Opinion and Memorandum Regulation, Actuarial Guideline 53 on reinvestment assumptions and Actuarial Standard of Practice 22

In-scope processes.value: Annual asset adequacy analysis for every in-force segment carrying interest and behaviour risk: segment definition, asset assignment, reinvestment and disinvestment strategy modelling, deterministic and stochastic scenario testing, sensitivity work, additional reserve determination and the asset adequacy documentation

In-scope systems.value: Cash-flow testing models and scenario generators, fed by the investment book of record for asset positions and cash flows; the asset adequacy report and its exhibits are held in the model governance repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Asset Adequacy Analysis Procedure — segmentation and asset assignment rules, scenario set definition, reinvestment and disinvestment assumption standard, deficiency measurement and additional reserve rules, sensitivity requirements and the report content standard

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary annually before the analysis starts, with the board risk committee informed of any change to the scenario set, the aggregation basis or the reinvestment assumptions

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual analysis as at 31 December supporting the opinion signed by 1 March; the asset adequacy memorandum prepared by 1 March and available to the commissioner by 1 July; the Regulatory Asset Adequacy Issues Summary by 15 March; the Actuarial Guideline 53 documentation on reinvestment assets filed on its own date of 1 April

Deadline reminders configured.value: Actuarial calendar opens asset assignment on 15 November with a preliminary run on the 30 September in-force, alerts the ALM actuary at the asset-lock and scenario-lock gates in January, and escalates to the Chief Actuary if the final run is not complete 15 days before 1 March

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Segment definitions, asset assignment listings, scenario sets, model runs with ids, scenario results, sensitivity results, additional reserve calculations and the asset adequacy report retained 7 years from the valuation date in the model governance repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Asset assignment breaks, segments tested on stale in-force, scenarios failing without an additional reserve, reinvestment assumptions outside the documented constraints and unreproducible runs are logged with the reserve effect and the correction

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Actuary signs off every additional reserve decision and every change to the reinvestment or disinvestment assumptions after the assumption lock

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every asset adequacy segment tested for the valuation year, the assets assigned to each, the scenario results produced and the additional reserves established, together with the segments excluded from testing and the basis for excluding them

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Assigned asset market value must reconcile to the investment book of record within 0.5 percent per segment with every break explained; any deficient scenario without either an additional reserve or a documented aggregation justification is a fail; a reinvestment assumption more favourable than the documented constraint is a fail regardless of the deficiency outcome

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual as at 31 December; the test runs once between the opinion signing and the 1 July memorandum availability date, with a preliminary review of the 30 September dry run so defects are found before the year-end cycle

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside the asset-liability and valuation production teams and must not have built or run any cash-flow testing model being reviewed

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual asset adequacy test workpaper — asset reconciliation, scenario reproduction, reinvestment assumption check, additional reserve recomputation and exception log — in the model governance repository under the valuation year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Asset adequacy memorandum with the segment, asset, scenario and sensitivity exhibits and the Actuarial Guideline 53 reinvestment documentation, producible for the domiciliary commissioner within 5 business days of a request and in any case by 1 July

Regulator response path.value: Appointed Actuary answers asset adequacy questions with the ALM / Asset-Liability Actuary supporting on the asset modelling; the Chief Actuary clears any response that would move an additional reserve and the board risk committee chair is informed

checklist.step: Define the segments to be tested and the basis for any exclusion
actions: List the in-force blocks by product family, guarantee type and investment segment and decide which are tested by cash-flow testing, which by a demonstration of a lesser method and which are excluded.

Justify each lesser method or exclusion in writing against the criteria — minimal interest sensitivity, short duration, immaterial reserve — and record the reserve amount involved so an examiner can see what was left out.

Confirm blocks with material interest, lapse or annuitisation optionality — payout annuities, deferred annuities with guaranteed minimum rates, universal life with secondary guarantees, structured settlements — are all cash-flow tested.
Agree the aggregation basis in advance: which segments may be aggregated for the deficiency conclusion and which must stand alone.
Have the Chief Actuary approve the segmentation and aggregation basis before assets are assigned.
checklist.done: every in-force block is assigned to a testing method with written justification for each exclusion and an approved aggregation basis.

checklist.step: Assign assets to segments and reconcile to the investment book of record
actions: Extract the asset positions at the valuation date with book value, market value, coupon, maturity, credit rating, call and prepayment features and asset class.
Assign assets to segments on the documented rule — segmented portfolio identifiers, or a pro rata allocation where the portfolio is not segmented — and record the rule applied per segment.
Reconcile assigned book and market value per segment and in total to the investment book of record and to Schedule D, requiring agreement inside 0.5 percent and explaining every break.
Confirm no asset is assigned to two segments and that unassigned surplus assets are identified separately rather than absorbed.
Sign the asset reconciliation before the asset-lock gate.
checklist.done: assigned assets reconcile to the investment book of record and Schedule D within 0.5 percent per segment, with no double assignment and a signed reconciliation.

checklist.step: Model the asset cash flows including embedded options
actions: Project coupon, principal and maturity cash flows for each asset, modelling call features, sinking funds and mortgage prepayment behaviour rather than assuming bullet maturities.
Apply the default cost and downgrade assumptions by rating and asset class from the documented table, and state the source used.
Model illiquid and complex assets — private placements, commercial mortgage loans, collateralised loan obligations, limited partnerships — explicitly, since these are where regulators focus.
Validate projected asset cash flows against the actual cash received in the prior year and explain material differences.
Record the asset model version and the run id with the assignment listing.
checklist.done: asset cash flows are projected with embedded options, documented default costs and explicit complex-asset modelling, validated against prior year actuals.

checklist.step: Set the reinvestment and disinvestment assumptions inside the guideline constraints
actions: Document the reinvestment strategy per segment: the asset mix, credit quality distribution, duration target and the spread assumed over the risk-free curve for reinvested assets.

Constrain the assumed net reinvestment spread to what the guideline permits, deducting assumed default costs and investment expenses, and show the gross to net derivation rather than stating a net figure.
Document the disinvestment strategy — which assets are sold first when cash is short, at what haircut, and whether borrowing is assumed.
Compare the assumed reinvestment mix to the actual purchases made in the last two years and justify any assumed shift to higher-yielding assets.
Prepare the Actuarial Guideline 53 documentation on projected reinvestment assets for the 1 April filing as this work is done, not afterwards.
checklist.done: reinvestment and disinvestment strategies are documented with a gross to net spread derivation inside the guideline constraint and compared to actual purchase behaviour.

checklist.step: Build the liability model and the policyholder behaviour assumptions
actions: Project liability cash flows from the same in-force extract used for the statutory valuation, and reconcile the starting reserve in the testing model to the certified statutory reserve per segment.
Set dynamic lapse, partial withdrawal, annuitisation and premium persistency assumptions that respond to the interest scenario, since static behaviour understates the risk the test exists to measure.
Model non-guaranteed elements — credited rates, cost of insurance charges, dividends — on the actual management policy and any contractual or practice constraint on changing them.
Model expenses on a going-concern basis with inflation, and state whether federal income tax is included and on what basis.
Record the liability model version, assumption set and run id.
checklist.done: liability cash flows start from the certified statutory reserve per segment and use dynamic behaviour, modelled non-guaranteed elements and stated expense and tax bases.

checklist.step: Run the deterministic scenario set
actions: Run the seven prescribed interest scenarios — level, gradually increasing, up then down, pop up then level, gradually decreasing, down then up, pop down then level — over the projection horizon.
Record for each scenario and segment the ending surplus, the pattern of interim deficiencies and the year of the worst position, not just the final number.
Confirm the projection horizon is long enough that the remaining business is immaterial or that a terminal provision is taken, and state which.
Store each scenario run with its run id and diagnostics so a specific scenario can be reproduced on request.
checklist.done: all seven prescribed scenarios are run per segment with ending and interim results recorded and each run reproducible by id.

checklist.step: Run the stochastic testing where the risk profile demands it
actions: Generate or take the prescribed economic scenarios and confirm the generator version, the calibration date and the number of paths used.
Run the stochastic projection for segments with material guarantees or path dependency and compute the distribution of ending surplus.
Measure the result at the stated conditional tail expectation level and compare it to the deterministic conclusion, explaining any divergence.
Test scenario count sufficiency by comparing results at reduced path counts and showing the metric has converged.
checklist.done: stochastic results are produced from a named, calibrated generator with a documented tail measure and evidence that the path count has converged.

checklist.step: Determine deficiencies and set any additional reserve
actions: Identify every scenario and segment where assets are inadequate to meet obligations under moderately adverse conditions, and quantify the shortfall.
Apply the approved aggregation basis and show the conclusion both before and after aggregation so the effect of aggregating is visible.
Compute the additional reserve required to remove the deficiency, state the method used to compute it, and confirm it is included in the filed statutory reserve.
Where no additional reserve is established despite a failing scenario, document the specific reasoning and have the Chief Actuary approve it in writing.
Reconcile the additional reserve to the reserve journal posted by the Controller.
checklist.done: every deficient scenario is quantified, aggregation effects are shown both ways, and each additional reserve is computed, posted and reconciled or explicitly approved as unnecessary.

checklist.step: Run the required sensitivity tests
actions: Re-run the analysis flexing the assumptions the conclusion is most exposed to — reinvestment spread, default cost, dynamic lapse elasticity, mortality improvement and expense inflation — one at a time.
Record the change in ending surplus and in any additional reserve for each flex, so the sensitivity is expressed in money rather than in adjectives.
Identify the assumption whose plausible movement would flip the conclusion and call it out explicitly in the report.
Run a combined adverse sensitivity where two related assumptions move together, since regulators ask for it when the single flexes look comfortable.
checklist.done: each key assumption has a single-flex sensitivity expressed in money, a combined adverse case is run, and the conclusion-flipping assumption is named.

checklist.step: Reconcile the testing model back to the statutory valuation
actions: Reconcile starting reserves in the testing model to the certified statutory reserves segment by segment and explain every difference above tolerance.
Reconcile the in-force counts and account values in the testing extract to the valuation extract used for the statutory reserve.
Reconcile assigned asset totals to the balance sheet invested assets so the test does not use assets the company does not hold.
Document each reconciliation as an exhibit to the asset adequacy report.
checklist.done: starting reserves, in-force and assigned assets in the testing model reconcile to the statutory valuation and the balance sheet, with exhibits attached.

checklist.step: Take the results to the Appointed Actuary and the board
actions: Present the asset adequacy conclusion by segment, the failing scenarios, the additional reserves and the sensitivity results to the board risk committee before the opinion is signed.
State the actuarial function view on the adequacy of technical provisions, the adequacy of pricing and the effect on capital, which ICP 8.7 expects to reach the board.
Flag any segment whose margin has narrowed materially against the prior year and say what management action is proposed.
Minute the committee receipt and record the minute reference on the analysis file.
checklist.done: the committee has received the conclusion, failing scenarios, additional reserves and sensitivities before the opinion is signed, with a minute reference recorded.

checklist.step: Write the asset adequacy report and the guideline documentation
actions: Write the report by 1 March covering segmentation, asset assignment and reconciliation, asset and liability modelling, scenario definitions, results by scenario and segment, sensitivities, additional reserves and the conclusion.

Complete the Actuarial Guideline 53 documentation on the projected reinvestment assets — the assumed mix, spreads, default costs and the comparison to actual investment practice — for filing by 1 April.
Include the prior year comparison and list every method and assumption change with its effect on the conclusion.
Have a second actuary review the report against the content standard and record the review before it is relied on for the opinion.
checklist.done: a peer-reviewed report prepared by 1 March covers all required sections, with the guideline documentation ready for the 1 April filing.

checklist.step: Feed the findings into pricing, ALM and reinsurance decisions
actions: Hand the segments with the narrowest margins to the Pricing Actuary with the specific assumption driving the strain, so new business pricing responds.
Hand the duration and reinvestment findings to the Chief Investment Officer with the target duration and asset mix implied by the testing.
Assess whether reinsurance could relieve a deficient segment and put the option to the Head of Reinsurance with the quantified benefit.
Record each referral with an owner and a date and follow it to a decision at the next quarterly actuarial review.
checklist.done: each narrow-margin or deficient segment is referred to pricing, investments or reinsurance with a quantified driver, an owner and a follow-up date.

checklist.step: Control post-signing changes to the analysis
actions: Lock the analysis, its runs and the report on the opinion signing date, allowing changes only as a dated addendum that states what changed and why.
Where an error is found after signing, quantify its effect on the additional reserve and on the opinion conclusion before deciding on any action.
Decide and record whether the opinion must be reissued, the memorandum amended or the correction carried into the next valuation, and inform the commissioner where a filed figure moves.
Raise a preventive fix with an owner and a date so the same defect does not recur.
checklist.done: the analysis is locked at signing, and any post-signing error carries a quantified effect, a recorded decision on reissue and a preventive fix.

checklist.step: Archive the asset adequacy evidence for reproduction
actions: Archive the segment definitions, asset assignment listing, asset and liability model versions, scenario sets, run ids, results, sensitivities, additional reserve calculations and the report.
Apply the 7-years-from-valuation-date retention label and mark the archive legal-hold-eligible.
Confirm the archive supports reproduction of any single scenario result from the recorded versions alone.
Index by valuation date, segment, scenario and run id so an examiner request for one failing scenario can be met without a re-run of everything.
checklist.done: the analysis is archived in a reproducible, scenario-level indexed form with a 7-year retention label applied.

testing.step: Build the population of segments, assets and scenario results
actions: Extract every segment tested, its testing method, its assigned asset market value, its starting reserve and its scenario results with run ids.
Extract the segments excluded from testing with the stated basis and the reserve amount each represents.
Reconcile tested plus excluded reserves to the total statutory reserve so no block is unaccounted for.
Sign the population as complete, recording the extract date, filters and record counts.
testing.done: tested and excluded segments together reconcile to the total statutory reserve and the population is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile assigned assets to the investment book of record
actions: Pull the asset positions at the valuation date independently and total book and market value by segment using the documented assignment rule.
Compare your totals to the assigned amounts and recompute the variance against the 0.5 percent tolerance rather than accepting the preparer reconciliation.
Test for double assignment by summing assigned market value across segments and comparing to total invested assets on the balance sheet and Schedule D.
List any segment tested on assets the company does not hold, or on assets counted twice, as an automatic exception.
testing.done: assigned assets are independently totalled per segment, variance is recomputed against tolerance and any double or phantom assignment is listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100 percent of segments with a failing scenario, an additional reserve, or a material narrowing of margin against the prior year.
Take 100 percent of segments excluded from cash-flow testing.
Take a seeded random sample of 6 remaining tested segments and, within each, 2 of the 7 prescribed scenarios.
Record the seed, population sizes, sample sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers all failing, reserved and excluded segments plus a reproducible random selection of segments and scenarios.

testing.step: Reproduce sampled scenario results from the recorded versions
actions: Restore the recorded asset model, liability model, assumption set and scenario definition for each sampled segment and scenario and re-run it yourself.
Compare your ending surplus and interim deficiency pattern to the reported result and require agreement inside the stated reproduction tolerance.
Where reproduction fails, determine whether the cause is an unrecorded version, a manual output adjustment or an untracked model change and name it.
Capture your run ids and diagnostics into the workpaper.
testing.done: sampled scenarios are re-run from recorded versions and either reproduce the reported result within tolerance or the failure cause is named.

testing.step: Challenge the reinvestment and disinvestment assumptions
actions: Recompute the assumed net reinvestment spread from the stated gross spread, default cost and investment expense and compare it to the guideline constraint.
Compare the assumed reinvestment asset mix and credit distribution to the actual purchases made in the last two years from the investment records and quantify any assumed shift.
Compare the assumed spreads to current market spreads for the same rating and tenor and flag any assumption above market without a documented basis.
Test the disinvestment assumption by checking the assumed sale haircut against observed transaction prices for comparable assets.
testing.done: the net reinvestment spread is recomputed against the constraint and the assumed mix, spreads and haircuts are benchmarked to actual purchases and market data.

testing.step: Test the liability model tie-out and the behaviour assumptions
actions: Tie the starting reserve in each sampled testing segment to the certified statutory reserve and quantify every difference.
Confirm lapse, withdrawal and annuitisation assumptions are dynamic by re-running one segment with the behaviour response switched off and quantifying the effect on the conclusion.
Check the credited rate and non-guaranteed element strategy modelled matches the actual management policy and any contractual floor.
Compare modelled expenses per policy to the actual expense study and flag any understatement.
testing.done: starting reserves tie to the certified valuation, dynamic behaviour is proven by a switch-off run, and credited rate and expense assumptions are validated against policy and study.

testing.step: Recompute the deficiency and additional reserve maths
actions: Recompute the deficiency for each sampled failing scenario from the projected cash flows and compare to the reported shortfall.
Recompute the additional reserve using the stated method and compare it to the amount included in the filed statutory reserve.
Recompute the conclusion before aggregation and confirm the aggregation applied matches the approved basis rather than a basis chosen after seeing the results.
List any failing scenario with neither an additional reserve nor a Chief Actuary approved written justification as a fail.
testing.done: deficiencies, additional reserves and the aggregation effect are independently recomputed and every unreserved failure without approved justification is a fail.

testing.step: Test the exclusions, the sensitivities and the report content
actions: For each excluded segment read the stated basis and test it against the criteria, checking the reserve amount excluded and whether interest sensitivity was genuinely immaterial.
Re-derive two reported sensitivity results from the underlying runs and compare to the report.
Confirm the report was prepared by 1 March from the document version history and that the Actuarial Guideline 53 reinvestment documentation was filed by 1 April with a receipt.
Confirm the report includes the prior year comparison and lists every method and assumption change with its effect.
testing.done: each exclusion is tested against the criteria, two sensitivities are re-derived, and the 1 March preparation and 1 April filing dates are evidenced.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the segment, the scenario, the amount involved and the effect on the additional reserve.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list — asset assignment break, asset double counted, stale in-force, static behaviour, reinvestment spread above constraint, aggregation changed after results, exclusion unjustified, run not reproducible — and name a single owner.
Set a remediation date and mark whether the exception changes the asset adequacy conclusion supporting the signed opinion.
Where the conclusion changes, notify the Appointed Actuary, the CFO and the board risk committee chair the same day and assess whether the opinion must be reissued.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a quantified reserve effect, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, and a same-day escalation where the conclusion moves.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the asset adequacy test
actions: State the results: segments reproduced within tolerance, asset reconciliations inside 0.5 percent, failing scenarios reserved, exclusions justified and sensitivities re-derived.
Write the conclusion — the asset adequacy analysis supports the opinion, supports it with exceptions, or does not support it — with the workpaper references behind each fail.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside the asset-liability and valuation teams and ran none of the tested models, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the board risk committee and to the Appointed Actuary before the 1 July memorandum availability date and file the workpaper in the model governance repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the reproduction, reconciliation and reserve results with a conclusion, reported to the committee and the Appointed Actuary before 1 July.
